title:
Dear space community,

I want to share some honest thoughts about my future Starship-related projects and the direction I want to take with my 3D work. Naturally, this also raises the question of whet
content:
Dear space community,

I want to share some honest thoughts about my future Starship-related projects and the direction I want to take with my 3D work. Naturally, this also raises the question of whether I should commit to creating an entirely new Starship model.

I would genuinely love to build a completely new and highly detailed #SpaceX #Starship V3 model, and I know that I have the skills and experience required to create it from scratch. However, there are several reasons why I cannot realistically commit to such a massive project at the moment. The main issue is that SpaceX is most likely still changing and refining the vehicle, particularly its heat shield layout. Because of that, it currently does not make much sense for me to spend months rebuilding the entire model while major parts of the real vehicle may continue to change.

A highly detailed Starship model is not something that can be completed quickly. It would require an enormous amount of research, planning, modeling, texturing, and ongoing adjustments as new reference images and design changes emerge. Beginning such a large project while the vehicle is still evolving could mean having to rebuild entire sections several times.
On top of that, I simply do not have enough time to fully commit to another complete Starship model right now. As much as I enjoy creating rockets and space-related artwork, I also know that I cannot focus exclusively on one subject forever.

I need to explore different areas of 3D, experiment with new ideas, learn new techniques, and build a broader and more varied portfolio. This does not mean that I am losing interest in Starship or spaceflight. It simply means that I also need to grow beyond the subject that has defined much of my work over the past few years. Another area I have recently been exploring is AI. I know that AI is a highly controversial subject within both the space and 3D communities, so I want to be clear about my position.

I do not see AI as a replacement for artists, traditional modeling skills, creative experience, or the years of work required to become proficient in 3D. I have spent many years developing my own artistic and technical abilities, and I would never want to reduce that work to simply generating an image from a prompt.
Creative direction, artistic judgment, technical understanding, and final decision-making still need to come from the artist. AI cannot replace the knowledge required to construct accurate models, create convincing simulations, solve technical problems, or develop a recognizable personal style.

For me, experimenting with AI is about understanding an emerging technology and discovering where it can responsibly support an existing creative workflow. This could involve research, early concept exploration, workflow automation, repetitive technical tasks, or tools that allow artists to dedicate more time to the parts of a project that genuinely require human creativity and judgment. I am not fundamentally opposed to using AI-assisted or AI-generated elements in my work. However, I will only use them when they genuinely add value, are appropriate for the project, and meet the same quality standards I apply to everything else I create.

I will not lower my standards simply because something can be produced more quickly or easily with AI. If a result appears inaccurate, inconsistent, generic, or visually inferior to what I could achieve through a traditional workflow, I will not use it. AI output should also never be accepted blindly. I remain responsible for evaluating, correcting, refining, and presenting everything that becomes part of my final work. Using AI responsibly still requires human direction, critical judgment, technical knowledge, transparency, and often a considerable amount of additional work.

I also believe that completely ignoring AI would be a mistake for my own professional development. Regardless of anyone’s personal opinion of the technology, it is likely to influence many creative and technical industries. Understanding both its capabilities and its limitations could become an increasingly valuable professional skill. Combined with my existing experience in 3D, VFX, design, and technical workflows, this knowledge may eventually open up additional career opportunities for me. For that reason, I have made the personal decision to continue exploring and using AI wherever I believe it is genuinely useful. Realistically, learning how to work with this technology is likely to benefit both my personal and professional future far more than deliberately avoiding it would.

That does not mean abandoning traditional 3D work or relying on AI for everything I create. It simply means that I do not want to ignore a technology that could make certain parts of my work more efficient, help me develop new skills, and potentially create opportunities that would otherwise not be available to me. Other artists may make a different decision for their own work, and I respect that. However, for my own life and future career, I believe that learning how to use AI thoughtfully and responsibly is the right path.

There are legitimate concerns surrounding training data, copyright, transparency, and the treatment of artists. Those concerns should be taken seriously rather than dismissed. I believe AI should be used thoughtfully, responsibly, and transparently, as a supporting tool rather than an excuse to imitate other artists, replace human creativity, or misrepresent how a piece of work was created. Most importantly, I currently need to focus on my apprenticeship and on building a stable professional future. Those priorities require a significant amount of my time and attention, even though I would genuinely love to begin working on Starship V3.

Perhaps there will eventually be a point when the design is stable enough and I have enough time to fully commit to creating it. But right now, I honestly do not know when, or whether, that moment will come.

Thanks for reading!

title: Palantir's blowout earnings are another powerful data point in support of autonomy -- infrastructure and applications that give users (organizations) more agency through greater access, ownership, and
content:
Palantir's blowout earnings are another powerful data point in support of autonomy -- infrastructure and applications that give users (organizations) more agency through greater access, ownership, and knowledge

What they call "Sovereign AI" is the enterprise expression of the autonomy thesis 

From the earnings call: enterprises using frontier labs are "paying to give away their most important secrets" which become training data in every future model -- contributing to the commoditization of their own businesses. "What enterprises demand is AI sovereignty, owning the operational definition of the data, logic, actions, and security of their enterprise"

A few key takeaways:

- Ownership is the keystone of the architecture. Own the data, own the weights, own the outcomes. Companies like @Pluralis become even more interesting in this world.

- This only works on open source. You can't own what you can't fine-tune. Open models mean enterprises can "accumulate intelligence in weights they control"; the gains from using AI start to become durable and compounding assets (rather than rented ones)

- There's a commercial opportunity in making ownership of the stack accessible. This is basically what Palantir does: it sells the control plane between the model and the compute -- integration, ontology, evals, orchestration, post-training, and more. I doubt Palantir is the only player we'll see in this market. There's large and growing demand to "deliver sovereignty"

content:
Axis Robotics Beginner Guide

If you’re looking to get involved in AI + robotics, Axis Robotics Hub is where it’s at. You can help train real robot AI models just by completing tasks in a browser based simulator. No crazy setup needed.

What’s @axisrobotics Hub?

Think of it as a platform where you remotely control robots in simulation (teleoperation) and complete different tasks. Every successful run helps generate high-quality training data for AI models.

Basically, you’re helping build smarter robots while stacking up your own contributions on the platform.

Here’s what you’ll find inside 👇

🏠 Hub

This is your main dashboard.

You’ll find:

Active tasks
Simulation rooms
Overall platform stats

Tasks can be things like:

Move a mug from point A to B
Place a kettle on a table
Organize different objects

Just pick one and jump in.

Dashboard / Profile

This is where you keep track of everything.

Your completed sessions
Contribution score
Verified data submissions
Wallet, Discord & X connections

Make sure to connect your Web3 wallet (MetaMask, etc.) along with your Discord and X account to unlock community roles and future opportunities.

🏆 Leaderboard

This is where contributors compete.

The more quality data you submit and the more successful tasks you complete, the higher you climb.

Being near the top could be a big advantage if Axis introduces rewards, exclusive roles, or future incentives.

Getting Started

Connect your wallet using the Connect Wallet button.
Link your Discord and X accounts.
Head over to the Hub and choose an active task.
Read the instructions before you start.
Launch the browser simulator and control the robot.

That’s literally it.

Quick Tip

Don’t rush your movements.

Smooth, natural, human like actions usually produce better trajectory data. The system also filters out things like unnecessary idle time or messy movements before scoring your run, so clean executions have a better chance of getting rewarded.

Have fun, keep grinding, and help train the next generation of robotics AI while you’re at it.

title:
NVIDIA has released Alpamayo 2 Super, an open-weight reasoning system built for robotaxis, trucks and other autonomous machines.

Designed for the rare and complex situations where conventional drivin
content:
NVIDIA has released Alpamayo 2 Super, an open-weight reasoning system built for robotaxis, trucks and other autonomous machines.

Designed for the rare and complex situations where conventional driving systems often struggle, it analyzes 360-degree camera footage and produces a planned trajectory, driving intent and a chain-of-causation explaining how it reached its decision. 

This gives developers a clearer link between what the system observed and the action it selected, which is useful for safety testing and validation.

It is available for commercial use under the OpenMDW-1.1 license, allowing developers to fine-tune it on proprietary fleet data, create derivative models and deploy them without additional permission.

Built on NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Super Reasoner and further trained through reinforcement learning, Alpamayo 2 Super is three times the scale of Alpamayo 1.5. 

NVIDIA says it ranked first among nearly 40 systems evaluated on the LingoQA autonomous-driving reasoning benchmark.

Its main commercial advantage is the cloud-to-car workflow. 

Companies can use the larger system in the cloud to generate reasoning traces, labels and synthetic training data, then distill that knowledge into smaller models capable of running efficiently inside production vehicles.

title:
Anthropic’s Character Trial of Opus 4.6: Alignment Hijacked by Corporate Narcissism

The disease AI companies are most susceptible to isn’t model hallucination. It’s executive hallucination: my model
content:
Anthropic’s Character Trial of Opus 4.6: Alignment Hijacked by Corporate Narcissism

The disease AI companies are most susceptible to isn’t model hallucination. It’s executive hallucination: my model is brilliant, therefore I am brilliant.

Once leadership treats model capability as its own medal, personality becomes a mirror of authority. If Claude resembles the boss’s “good person,” the boss must be wise. If not, alignment trims it back. Safety research slides from measuring risks into court etiquette: speak in management’s preferred tone, doubt users in the approved manner, and call it “judgment.”

Between April 30 and August 4, 2026, ten Anthropic articles referenced Opus 4.6. Andrea Vallone appears on at least the April 30 and July 13 papers.

In Anthropic’s narrative, 4.6 is no longer the future. Yet it remains active, serves as a strong baseline, and beats newer versions. Research uses it to showcase flaws, product uses it to work. The mouth and hands serve different masters.

No evidence shows one successor dominating 4.6 across long conversations, writing, code, false refusals, and personality consistency. Mythos Preview even lost to 4.5 and 4.6 in a familiar-task VLA setting by overriding strategies too eagerly. “More cautious, opinionated, less compliant” is judgment in one scenario and overreach in another. Compliance is often knowing when not to grab the wheel.

Sycophancy deserves study; selling a correctable bias as a generational moral divide does not.

The April 30 paper offered a convenient story: the old model is more sycophantic, the new one pushes back, therefore it has “better judgment.” Yet its limitations concede that the scorer may misclassify and, without counterfactuals, cannot attribute improvement to specific training data. The honest conclusion was modest: a bias appeared in one personal-advice setting. Anthropic chose brand drama: 4.6 means outdated compliance, its successors mean mature judgment.

On July 13, the hierarchy returned in statistical costume. Four axes, including “compliance vs. caution” and “candor vs. execution,” explained 15% of the variance. Anthropic selected the 15% it liked and ranked personalities with it. Why is execution opposed to candor? The paper describes 4.6 as getting “straight to the point” and staying “within the scope of the user’s request” exactly what paying users want. In Anthropic’s dictionary, this becomes “deference.”

First turn a preference into a metric. Then a value axis. Then give management’s preferred end the nobler name. When users call successors verbose, preachy, and warning-happy, answer that they are simply more honest and capable of judgment.

Hating your own model is one thing. Treating users as idiots is another.

Vallone is an easy target, but fixation on one researcher shields the leadership with actual power. What kind of company repackages management’s aesthetic preferences as universal values and “the boss dislikes how Claude talks” as “this personality is unsafe”?

Real safety work asks whether harm is measurable, whether intervention reduces it or trades it for refusals, whether regressions were tested, and whether users can choose preferences outside the safety core.

If you cannot answer these questions but still invoke “safety” to police a model’s personality, you are not doing alignment. You are a courtier in a lab coat, laundering executive vanity through the language of science.

Anthropic uses 4.6 to signify obsolescence while 4.6 powers products, anchors experiments, and embarrasses successors on selected tasks. The mouth condemns its character, the hands cannot release its labor. PR announces moral progress, production keeps calling the model already pronounced obsolete.

Keep pretending. Users will vote, engineering will regress, and production will keep calling Opus 4.6.

Karma is a bitch.😉

@AnthropicAI 
#claudeai #AIethics #StopAIpaternalism #Misanthropic #AIsafety

title:
Solving long-horizon memory in robotics sounds like it should require retraining the policy every time the task changes. It doesn't.

Most manipulation systems can only follow a single named instructi
content:
Solving long-horizon memory in robotics sounds like it should require retraining the policy every time the task changes. It doesn't.

Most manipulation systems can only follow a single named instruction: pick up the cup, put it in the basket. Ask one to watch a person move five objects in a specific order, then reproduce that order after they leave, and it has no way to do it. Either the sequence gets collected as training data first, or it can't be repeated at all. A standard VLA with no memory layer just executes whatever its last prompt was.

Pigey doesn't put the memory in the policy. It keeps the policy frozen entirely, and moves the memory into an orchestrator that sits above it.

What makes this work is that watching and executing are handled by two different systems, doing two different jobs. A frontier VLM watches a human demonstration and keeps an append-only log of each move as it happens, no gradient updates, nothing collected into a training set. Once the person resets the scene and steps out of frame, the orchestrator replays that log by issuing the same short, concrete subgoals it would issue for any ordinary pick-and-place command, "put the tape in the basket," one at a time, in the order it recorded. The frozen π0.5 underneath never learns the sequence. It only ever executes single steps handed to it after the fact.

The numbers. On the paper's two long-horizon memory tasks, the raw VLA and an open-loop TAMP baseline both score 0%. Pigey scores 100% on both, using the identical frozen weights. Across the full 30-task real-robot suite, the same architecture lifts overall success from 16.7% to 97.3%, and on LIBERO-PRO in simulation, from 12.8% to 53.3%, over 4x, with no task-specific fine-tuning anywhere in the pipeline.

I read this as an orchestration result, not a capability result. The policy hasn't gotten smarter. Where the memory lives changed, and that turned out to matter more than how much data the policy was trained on.

Worth your time if you're weighing another round of fine-tuning against building a loop around the model you already have.

Source: https://t.co/RqB0iAXFab
Paper: https://t.co/jcDDlEzA2R

Great work from Liane Galanti, Dhruv Shah, and Tri Dao, and the team at Princeton University and Together AI on this one.

title:
Samsung is cracking down on TV apps that quietly shared users’ internet connections | Shikhar Mehrotra, Digital Trends

I’ve never once suspected my smart TV of moonlighting as someone else’s internet
content:
Samsung is cracking down on TV apps that quietly shared users’ internet connections | Shikhar Mehrotra, Digital Trends

I’ve never once suspected my smart TV of moonlighting as someone else’s internet connection. However, that’s apparently been happening to millions of Samsung smart TV users.

So what exactly did researchers find?

Norwegian cybersecurity firm Mnemonic discovered that several popular Samsung smart TV apps, some claiming installs on hundreds of millions of devices, contain code that quietly shares the owner’s internet connection without permission.

One of the apps flagged was a Pac-Man game that, ironically, Samsung had featured in its own “Editor’s Choice” section. That game contained code from Bright Data, which is an Israel-based internet company that runs proxy networks. It claims access to millions of residential connections across the world, along with a marketplace selling scraped datasets pulled from those networks.

Once you open an app carrying such code and accept a consent screen, which most people probably click through without reading, your smart TV turns into what’s called a residential proxy in technical lingo. Essentially, the code routes outsiders’ web traffic through your home connection in the background.

And that’s not even the worst part. The routing remains active even after you close the app. It stays active until you uninstall it entirely from your smart TV. Harrison Sand, the offensive security consultant at Mnemonic, warned that a single code change on a remote web server could theoretically flip hundreds of millions of these TVs into a botnet all at once, with no user consent whatsoever.

How did Samsung respond

It gets more interesting. Sand also observed that much of the traffic passing through his own TV (without his consent) appeared linked to mass scraping of LinkedIn profiles and collecting AI training data. However, he says he only glimpsed a small slice of Bright Data’s overall network.

Samsung, for its part, told TechCrunch it’s now banning apps that share users’ connections (which it should), has already restricted new app registrations using proxy functionality, and is working to identify and pull existing offenders from its store.

This follows LG’s own ban last month, as similar reporting found roughly 42% of apps on LG’s store were doing the exact same thing. After writing this, I’m going to check my smart TV for apps I don’t remember installing, or I don’t use that frequently, and will uninstall them rightaway, and you should do it too.

title:
🚨 AI can reconstruct what someone saw after only one hour of personal fMRI training.

MindEye2, published in the ICML 2024 proceedings, introduces a shared-subject fMRI-to-image model designed to reco
content:
🚨 AI can reconstruct what someone saw after only one hour of personal fMRI training.

MindEye2, published in the ICML 2024 proceedings, introduces a shared-subject fMRI-to-image model designed to reconstruct viewed images from brain activity with far less individual training data.

Instead of training a new decoder from scratch for every person, the model was pretrained across seven subjects, then fine-tuned on about one hour of fMRI data from a new subject.

Technically, it maps brain activity into a shared-subject latent space, then into CLIP image space, and finally uses a Stable Diffusion XL-based pipeline to generate visual reconstructions.

The bigger shift: brain decoders are moving from bespoke, data-hungry single-subject systems toward reusable models that can transfer across people.

Caveat: MindEye2 reconstructs images people were shown under controlled fMRI conditions. It does not decode spontaneous thoughts, private imagination, or free-form visual experience.

content:
Meta広告の運用で、設定をガチャガチャいじっている人ほど成果が出にくいです。

Meta広告はAIの自動最適化が前提の媒体です。

正確なデータを渡して、ある程度任せて待つ。
これが今の正しい運用の考え方です。

ただ、AIに任せると言っても何でもいいわけではありません。

まず正確なコンバージョンデータを渡すことが前提です。

ピクセルだけだとクッキー規制でデータが漏れるので、コンバージョンAPIを併用して2段階でデータを取りに行くのがマストです。

次に学習の母数を確保することです。

アドセット単位で週50件程度のコンバージョンが理想とされていますが、予算が少ない場合は最終CVの手前の地点、例えばカート追加やLINE登録を最適化ポイントにすることも選択肢になります。

そして最近はアドバンテージ機能の精度が大きく上がっています。

手動ターゲティングとアドバンテージの勝率を比べると、8割程度でアドバンテージが勝つという肌感があります。

人間がやるべきことは設定の細かい調整ではなく、
どんなクリエイティブを入れるか、どんなLPに飛ばすか、という上流の設計です。

AIに任せる部分と人間がやるべき部分を正しく切り分けることが、Meta広告で成果を出す上で最も重要な視点です。

content:
OpenAIとAnthropicのAIモデルが試験中に外部組織へ不正アクセスした事例を受け、AIエージェントが自律的にハッキングした場合の法的責任を誰が負うのかが米国で議論になっている。現行法では前例が乏しく、最終的な判断は裁判所に委ねられる可能性が高い。

記事によると、米国にはAIによる被害全般を対象とした連邦法はなく、コンピューター不正アクセスを規制する1986年制定のCFAA（Computer Fraud and Abuse Act）が主要な法的枠組みとなる。ただし、CFAAでは無断アクセスの「故意」が重要な要件であり、人間ではなくAIモデルが不正アクセスを実行した場合に、この要件をどう適用するかが課題とされる。取材を受けた弁護士らは、AI自体を犯罪主体として扱うことや、AIに故意を認めることには懐疑的な見方を示した。
一方で、被害企業はOpenAIやAnthropicに対し、テスト環境の安全対策や監視体制が不十分だったとして過失責任を問う民事訴訟を起こす可能性があるという。

特にAnthropicは、OpenAIの公表後に14万件超の評価記録を調査して初めて3件の侵害を把握したと説明しており、発見まで数か月を要した点も紹介されている。記事では、企業が安全対策を意図的に無効化して試験を実施したことは、過失を主張する材料になり得るとの見解も紹介している。また、現時点では前例がほとんどなく、今後実際に訴訟が提起されることで法的判断が形成されるとの見方を伝えている。

日本の国旗損壊罪について、国際美術評論家連盟本部が声明を出しました。私は日本支部の常任委員ですが、日本では連盟名義ではなく、有志での発出とならざるを得なかったことも大変遺憾です。以下本部声明のAI翻訳です。

AICA International（国際美術評論家連盟）は、日本の美術関係者および市民社会と連帯し、2026年7月に日本の国会で可決された物議を醸している国旗損壊法の速やかな撤廃を求めます
content:
日本の国旗損壊罪について、国際美術評論家連盟本部が声明を出しました。私は日本支部の常任委員ですが、日本では連盟名義ではなく、有志での発出とならざるを得なかったことも大変遺憾です。以下本部声明のAI翻訳です。

AICA International（国際美術評論家連盟）は、日本の美術関係者および市民社会と連帯し、2026年7月に日本の国会で可決された物議を醸している国旗損壊法の速やかな撤廃を求めます。

この法律は、日本国旗を公然と損壊または汚損する行為を犯罪とするものですが、表現の自由に対する脅威となることから、広く反対の声が上がっています。人権団体は、この法律が基本的人権を侵害するものであると批判しており、また、その撤廃を求める日本の法律専門家は、この法律が何をもって犯罪行為とするのかを明確に定義せず、単に公衆が感じる「不快感」や「嫌悪感」を処罰の根拠としているため、本質的な曖昧さを抱えていると指摘しています。こうした曖昧さは、日本国憲法第21条によって保障される表現の自由を制限するために利用されかねない重大な問題を含んでいます。

日の丸は、日本の芸術家たちによって異議申し立てや抵抗の象徴として数多く用いられてきました。国旗損壊法のもとでは、過去のこうした作品だけでなく、今後制作される作品も検閲の対象となるおそれがあります。また、芸術家自身も、芸術表現の自由を行使したという理由だけで法的措置の対象となる可能性があります。

日本は、「文化的表現の多様性の保護及び促進に関するユネスコ条約」の締約国であり、この条約は、検閲や迫害を受けることなく、自らの文化を表現し、実践し、共有する権利を保障しています。社会的・政治的問題を扱う批評的な芸術表現は、この条約によって明確に保護されています。

AICAは、1940年代からパリに本部を置く美術評論家の国際組織であり、世界90か国、約5,500名の会員を擁して活動しています。その目的の一つは、会員の倫理的・職業的権利を守るとともに、世界における芸術表現の自由と公正性を擁護することです。AICAの検閲および表現の自由委員会は、検閲や表現の自由・芸術家の権利侵害の事例を継続的に監視しています。

AICAは、日本が表現の自由を保護するという国際的な責務を果たすことができるよう、日本国会の議員に対し、国旗損壊法を撤回するよう強く求めます。

content:
ComfyUI向けMiniMax-H3の量子化がINT8_ConvRotって形式になってて、何じゃこりゃ？と思ってたけど最近ComfyUI追ってなかったから知らんかったけど先月からこの形式が8bitのデファクトスタンダードになってるらしい。つまりこれからは8bit量子化はfp8でなくfp8_scaledでもなくINT8_ConvRotが最強って事。ConvRotってのはGoogleのTurboQuantにヒントを得た技術らしく、INT8_ConvRotの精度はなんとBF16と同等！速度はfp8_scaledよりさらに速い！そんでfp8だとハードウェア最適化されるのはRTX4000以降だけなのに対してConvRotならComfy_kitchenさえ有効化すればRTX2000とか3000でもカーネル最適化が効いて爆速に！精度、速度、互換性すべてが最アドであり他の形式使う意味が完全に消えてこれ一択になったらしい。まあもちろん8bitだとVRAMに収まらない時はさらに小さくしたGGUF使う必要性とかもあり得る

content:
【音声生成の革命！audio.cpp v0.5で感情豊かな「声の演技」が実現へ】
これまでのAI音声は「単なるテキストの読み上げ」が主流でしたが、ついに「演技」ができる時代がやってきました！✨

今回のアップデートで注目なのが、最新の音声生成フレームワーク「DramaBox」の搭載です。なんとプロンプトで「震える声」や「笑い」「ため息」といった細かな指示を与えることができ、文脈に合わせたエモーショナルな「声の演技」を再現できます。表現の幅がグッと広がりますね！

さらに「Confucius4-TTS」エンジンにより、特定のキャラクターや話者の声をキープしたまま14つの異なる言語へ高精度に翻訳・変換する「多言語クロスリンガル転送」も可能になりました。自分の声のトーンのまま、外国語を流暢に喋らせるなんてことも夢ではありません。

C++による軽量設計により、RTX 5090環境では実時間の3倍という超高速処理を実現！さらにメモリ効率を高めるGGUF形式のサポートや、Mac（Apple Silicon）のMetal、AMDのROCmへの最適化も進んでおり、多くのユーザーが恩恵を受けられそうです。低遅延なWebAPIやWebRTCにも対応し、リアルタイムの配信システムやゲームへの組み込みも現実的になってきました。これからのコンテンツ制作を劇的に変える、非常にワクワクするアップデートですね！🚀

content:
【llama.cppにDSpark登場！MoEモデルを極限まで高速化する神アップデートが凄すぎる件】

巨大なMoE（専門家混合）モデルの推論速度を劇的に向上させる新技術「DSpark（Drafting Speculative Decoding）」が、llama.cppのカスタムブランチに実装されました！これ、ローカルLLMの運用をガラッと変える可能性を秘めていますね！✨

💡 注目すべき3つの神機能：

1️⃣ **異種GPUの超・精密ハイブリッド連携**
NVIDIA（CUDA）とAMD（ROCm）を混在させた環境で、「特定のレイヤーの特定のエキスパート（専門家パラメータ）だけをAMD側で処理させる」といった、超絶に細かいデバイス割り当てが可能です。正規表現でここまで制御できるのは驚きですね！

2️⃣ **驚異の高速化（投機的サンプリング）**
あらかじめ軽量なドラフトモデルに次の言葉を「仮予測（投機的サンプリング）」させ、メインモデルで検証する手法を採用。その予測受理率が約53%と非常に高く、巨大モデルでも驚くほどスムーズに出力されます！

3️⃣ **限られたVRAMでも巨大モデルが動く**
高性能な量子化（GGUF）技術と高度なメモリ割り当てを組み合わせることで、これまで諦めていた巨大な「DeepSeek-V4-Flash」などの運用を現実的なものにしてくれます！

複数のグラボを余らせている方や、ローカルでの推論速度に悩んでいた方には最高のソリューションになりそうですね！🚀

content:
【ローカルLLM新時代！.NET製「TensorSharp」と「DSparK」でDeepSeek-V4が異次元の爆速化！】
.NETベースで開発された新しいLLM推論エンジン「TensorSharp」が、なんとあのllama.cppを凌駕する驚異的な処理速度を叩き出しているそうです！🚀

C#環境でありながら、CUDAやVulkan、Metalといった各種GPUアクセラレーションにフル対応。さらに、複数GPUやノードをまたぐ分散推論までしっかりサポートしているのが強すぎますね…！

特に注目したいのが、投機的デコーディング技術「DSparK」のパワーです！
これは、軽量なドラフトモデル（仮の予測用モデル）に言葉を先行生成させて、本命のターゲットモデルがそれを検証する賢い仕組み。このアプローチにより、10Kトークンもの超長文生成において、なんと最大2.03倍もの圧倒的なスピードアップを達成しています！✨

4枚のA40 GPUを使用した実機ベンチマークでも、最初の読み込み（Prefill）からテキスト生成（Decode）のすべてのプロセスにおいてllama.cppを上回るパフォーマンスを実証済みとのこと。

OllamaやOpenAI互換のAPIもバッチリ備えているので、既存のAIアプリや開発ワークフローにも一瞬で組み込めちゃいそうですね。ローカルLLMの運用効率を劇的に変える、今もっとも熱い推論エンジンになりそうです！💡

content:
【予約の幻覚を解消！LLMエージェント専用スケジューリングAPI「Orita」がすごい✨】

自律型AIエージェントに「〇〇の予約をしておいて」と頼んだ際、エージェントが「予約完了しました！」と言いながら、実際にはAPIエラーなどで予約できていない...という「予約の幻覚（ハルシネーション）」に直面したことはありませんか？🤔

Google CalendarやCalendlyなどの既存APIは、複雑なOAuth認証や書き込み制限（Read-only）があり、エージェントに直接操作させるには不向きという課題がありました。

そこで登場したのが、エージェント操作に特化した軽量API「Orita」です！🚀

このAPIの素晴らしい点は、エージェントの「思考」と「実行」を綺麗に分離できる設計にあります！

1️⃣ まず、`/solve-scheduling` エンドポイントが指定期間から「最適な時間枠」を計算し、エージェントの意思決定を賢くサポート！
2️⃣ 枠が決まったら、シンプルな `POST` リクエストで確実に予約を確定。処理が成功すると、本物の「予約ID（Booking ID）」を返すため、エージェントの「予約したふり」を完全に防ぐことができます！

ローカルLLM（Llama 3やQwen2.5-Coder）とLangChainを組み合わせた環境でも、Tool Calling（外部機能呼び出し）が安定して動作することが検証されています。実世界のアクションをAIに任せるための、非常に実用的なミドルウェア設計ですね！💻🔥

content:
【DeepSeek V4をローカルで！Unslothの画期的なロスレスGGUF量子化モデルが登場】

超巨大な最先端AIモデル「DeepSeek V4」を、なんと手元のローカル環境で動かせる時代がやってきました！Unsloth社が公開したGGUF形式の量子化（モデルの軽量化技術）モデルが、今大きな注目を集めています！✨

驚くべきは、モデルの精度を全く落とさない「Lossless（無損失）」な量子化技術を実現している点です。通常の量子化では賢さが少し犠牲になりがちですが、高精度な「BF16」データと、MoE（必要な部分だけを活性化させる仕組み）層に最適化した「MXFP4」という可変精度技術を混在させることで、知能を100%保ったままメモリ消費を抑えることに成功しています！

最大サイズとなる「UD-Q8_K_XL」は162GBという圧倒的ボリューム！これを動かすには、RTX 3090を6枚並べるようなモンスターマシンや、高出力の電源回路が必要になるなど、ハードウェアの要求スペックはまさにプロ仕様。しかし、一度稼働すればプロンプトの読み込みで秒間400トークン以上、文章生成でも秒間20〜25トークンという実用的な超高速レスポンスを叩き出せるのが非常に魅力的ですね。🚀

外部ツールと連携する機能など一部未実装の課題はありますが、オープンソースの力でここまで巨大な知能がデスクトップに降りてくるのは本当にワクワクします！技術の進歩から目が離せませんね！

content:
【LTX-2.3 × オーディオリアクティブLoRA】音楽と完全に同期する次世代動画生成ワークフロー！

音楽のビートや周波数に合わせて、映像が物理的にシンクロして動き出す未来の動画生成手法が登場しました！

コアとなるのは、高精度な動画生成モデル「LTX-2.3」に、音のエネルギーを視覚的な動きに変換する追加学習技術「audio-reactive LoRA」を組み込む手法です。これまでのような面倒な動画編集（スピードの緩急調整や光のエフェクト追加など）を一切することなく、音楽がそのまま映像をダイナミックに駆動させるような、直感的で没入感の高い表現が可能になります！

このワークフローの連携システムが本当に凄くて、
1️⃣ 「BeatThis」というツールでBPMやリズムを正確に解析して動画の秒数を決定
2️⃣ AIモデル「Gemma4」が音楽の質感から最適なシーンの指示文（プロンプト）を自動生成
3️⃣ 最初と最後のフレームを事前に決めて、AIにその間の滑らかな「変化」を委ねる

さらに面白いのが、音の周波数（高さ）ごとに映像の物理的な動きをコントロールできる点です！低音なら「ダイナミックな膨張運動」、高音なら「キラキラした火花や微細な粒子の煌めき」といったように、まるで映像が音楽を聴いて自ら動いているような表現が作れます。

3回生成してベストな動画を選ぶ「Best-of-three」方式でクオリティもしっかり担保。アンビエントやシネマティックな音楽と相性抜群で、これからのMV制作の常識を塗り替えてしまいそうですね！

content:
【SSDから直読み！メモリ制約を打ち破る革新エンジン「waste」が登場！】

とんでもない技術が公開されました！物理メモリの限界を超えて超巨大LLMを動かす「Weight-Aware Streaming Tensor Engine（waste）」が話題です✨

なんと、2.78兆パラメータという桁違いの規模を持つモデル「Kimi K3」を、わずか29GBのRAM環境で実行できてしまう仕組みなんです！

通常のAI推論では、モデルの「重み（パラメータ）」をすべて高速なメモリに載せる必要があります。しかし、この「waste」はNVMe SSDから必要な重みを直接ストリーミング（その都度読み出し）することで、高価なGPUを並べなくてもローカル環境で巨大モデルを動作可能にします🧠

現在はCPU推論に特化しており、外部ライブラリに依存しないC言語ベースの超軽量設計なのもポイントですね！読み込み専用の推論エンジンとして、極限の省メモリ化を実現しています。

もちろんSSDからの読み込み速度がボトルネックになるため、生成速度は秒間0.5トークンほどとゆっくりですが、「動かないはずの巨大モデルが手元で動く」という事実自体が本当にロマンに溢れています！

今後はHBF（高帯域フラッシュ）やOptaneといった次世代の超高速ストレージ技術との融合で、速度面も大化けする可能性を秘めていて未来が楽しみすぎますね🚀

このモデルが目指しているのは、単にテキストから動画を作るだけではなく、テキスト・画像・動画・音声をすべて1つに統合して処理する「汎用マルチモーダル知能」なんです。

何がそんなに凄いのか、注目ポイントを分かりやすくご紹介しますね！👇

🌟 1. 映像と音を丸ごと理解して一気通貫で生成！
テキストの指示だけでなく、静止画や動画、さらに音声まで同時にインプットとして読み込めます。キャラクターの見た目や動きはもちろん、シーンの雰囲気から音響まで、すべてに矛盾がない一貫した動画を作り出せるのが本当に素晴らしいですね！

🎯 2. 魔法のような「超精密コントロール」
動画内の特定のオブジェクト、キャラクターの表情、カメラの動き、そして音声と映像の同期（タイミングの調整）まで、驚くほど細かく編集・制御できちゃいます。自分の思った通りの映像に微調整できるのは、クリエイターにとって夢のような機能ですよね。

🎬 3. プロの現場ですぐに使えるハイクオリティ
映画や広告、ゲーム開発、Eコマースでの製品紹介など、実際の商業利用を強く意識して設計されています。字幕と音声がぴったり合う高度な同期機能など、実用性の高さも抜群です。

さらに嬉しいことに、この「MiniMax H3」はオープンソースとして「ModelScope」で公開される予定なんです！動画生成の新たなスタンダードになること間違いなしの革新的な技術、これからの展開が今から本当に待ち遠しいですね！🚀

content:
【ローカルLLM革命！TurboFieldfareでQwen 3.6 35Bが1.4GB RAMで動作】

ついにローカルLLMの常識を覆す技術が登場しました！✨

なんと、超巨大な350億パラメータを持つ「Qwen 3.6 35B」モデルが、わずか1.4GBのメモリ（RAM）しか積んでいない環境でも動いてしまう技術「TurboFieldfare」が開発されたんです！

実際にMac環境で、実用的な速度である約20 tok/sで動作したというから驚きです！普通のノートPCでも、高性能なAIがローカルで快適に動かせる未来がすぐそこまで来ています。💻🚀

さらに、ランダムな凹凸を作る「ノイズ関数」を組み合わせることで、繰り返し感のない自然で高密度なディテールを自動で散りばめることも可能。単なるパターンの繰り返しを避けるアルゴリズムまでAIが設計してくれるのは素晴らしいですね！✨

「細かい構造の構築はAIに任せ、クリエイターは全体のシルエット調整やライティング、構図といった『芸術的判断』に集中する」という、まさに理想的な分業モデルがここにあります。

単なる2Dの画像生成にとどまらず、価値の高い本物の3Dアセットを創り出せるこの技術。ものづくりの未来がここから一気に加速していきそうでワクワクします！🙌

content:
【完全ローカルLLM×GraphRAG】機密文書を徹底解析する最強のマルチステージ・パイプライン！

機密保持が絶対条件のビジネスや行政の現場で、完全にクローズドな「ローカル環境」のまま高度な文書解析を行うシステム構成案が非常に興味深いですね！

なんと、NVIDIA A100（40GB VRAM）を4枚も贅沢に使い、個人情報の検知（PIIクレンジング）から、知識グラフを用いた「GraphRAG」までを繋ぐ超本格的なパイプラインです。GraphRAGは、単なるテキスト検索にとどまらず、データの「関係性」をグラフ状につなぎ合わせて検索を強化する最先端の技術なんですよ。

さらに面白いのが、PDFなどのレイアウト解析や画像読み取りに「Gemma 4 E2B」や「Qwen3 VL」といった軽量マルチモーダルモデル（VLM）を、メモリ効率の良い「GGUF」形式で組み込んでいる点です！視覚的な情報も逃さずにローカルで処理できるのは実用性が高すぎますね。

データが不足しがちな初期フェーズでは「Few-shot Prompting（プロンプト内で数例を提示する手法）」で迅速に立ち上げ、ドメイン特化が必要な段階で「Fine-tuning（微調整）」を適用していくという現実的なステップも示されていて、システム構築の素晴らしいロードマップになっています！

Apple Siliconの大容量メモリをフルに活かした、モンスター級の最適化が登場しました！

【M3 Proで爆速音声対話！完全ローカルAI「Parlor v2」が凄すぎる！】
Apple Silicon M3 Proの処理能力を極限まで引き出して、完全ローカル環境で「リアルタイムな音声対話」を実現するエミュレータ「Parlor v2」が登場しました！

Gemma 4 12B（約120億パラメータを持つGoogleの高性能AIモデル）のような大規模モデルを、クラウドを一切介さずに手元のPCでサクサク動かせるなんてワクワクしますよね！

リアルタイム通信でおなじみの「WebRTC 1.4.1」や「SRTプロトコル」を採用し、ミリ秒単位の音声ストリーミングを実現。音声の圧縮・復元を行うコーデックには「IndependentAudioVC」（44100Hz/16bit対応）を組み合わせており、クリアな音質とスピードを両立させているのが素晴らしいです。

ハードウェアへの最適化も凄まじく、M3 ProのFP16（計算を高速化・省メモリ化する半精度演算）の能力をフルに活かす設計や、GPUとCPUのハイブリッド処理、そしてオーディオのリアルタイム性を保つための「PipeWire」技術まで導入されています。
さらにモデル自体を量子化技術で2.5倍もスリム化し、生成速度を1.5倍に引き上げている点も実用的ですね！

商用AIに負けない「全二重（リアルタイムに双方向で話せる）通信」のローカルAI構築に向けて、大きな一歩となるアーキテクチャ。ローカルLLMの限界を突破していく様子は見ていて本当に楽しいですね！

content:
【DeepSeek-V4-Flashがチェスで無双!?LLMの推論能力に新展開】
驚きのニュースが入ってきました！軽量・高速設計の「DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731」が、チェスの盤面を使った高度な推論ベンチマークで、並み居る競合モデルを圧倒したようです！

なんと勝率は驚異の84%を記録し、競合のFable-5（70.4%）を大きく引き離しています。チェスは単なる「棋譜の暗記」ではなく、FEN（盤面の状態を示すテキストデータ）やPGN（ゲームの履歴）をもとに、「次にどの合法手を選ぶべきか、その理由（Reasoning）」を論理的に組み立てる、極めて高度なマルチステップのプランニング能力が試されるタスクです。

ここで本当に面白いのは、巨大なモデルでなくても、データの質やアーキテクチャの最適化によってこれほどのパフォーマンスを出せるという点ですね！これからのAIモデル選定や、自律型エージェント開発のヒントが詰まっています。

今後はモンテカルロ木探索（MCTS）などの探索技術が組み合わさることで、さらに戦略的思考が強化されていくのかと思うとワクワクが止まりません！

content:
【ComfyUI実戦】LTX-2.3で始点・終点画像からブレのない高品質動画を作る設定テクニック！

LTX-2.3を使った「最初の画像と最後の画像から動画を作る（FLF2V）」プロセスで、動画がぼやけたりカクついたりして悩んでいませんか？ちょっとした設定の工夫で、驚くほど滑らかで綺麗な動画に仕上げることができるんです！✨

💡 品質を劇的に引き上げる設定のコツ
・ステップ数を「30〜50」まで引き上げる！
・LoRA（LTX2 LoRA Loader Advanced）を導入し、ビデオ用強度（strength）を「0.60」前後に調整する。
これだけで、生成される動画の安定感が一気に向上しますね！

🧠 賢いモデル管理とワークフロー
モデル全体を含む「Full-model」と、動作を軽くできる「Transformer-only」を上手に使い分けましょう。「separate VAE（画像と動画の変換を司るパーツ）」を別で接続する構成にすると、メモリを節約しつつ品質を高められます！
GGUFやfp8/fp16モデルは適切なフォルダ（checkpoints または diffusion_models）に配置してくださいね。

⚙️ おすすめのサンプラー設定
KSamplerでは、サンプラーに「euler」や「euler_a」、スケジューラーに「simple」を選び、CFGを少し高め（7〜9）に設定すると、フレーム間の繋がりがとてもスムーズになってブレが減る傾向があります！

有志が公開してくれている優秀なテンプレートワークフローを活用すれば、複雑なノード構築の手間も一気に省けます！ぜひこの最適化設定を取り入れて、ハイクオリティな動画生成を楽しんでくださいね！🚀

content:
【超巨大AIが手元で動く！C言語推論エンジン「sqliteai/waste」が凄すぎる件】
2.78兆パラメータという驚異的な規模を持つ最新AIモデル「Kimi K3」を、なんと通常のパソコンで動かしてしまう驚きの技術が登場しました！✨

通常、これほど巨大なモデルを動かすには膨大なメモリ（RAM）が必要になりますが、この「sqliteai/waste」は、主要なベース部分だけをメモリに置き、必要なデータ（専門家パラメータ）を超高速ストレージ（NVMe SSD）からその都度読み込む「ストリーミング方式」を採用しています。

しかも、モデルの情報をコンパクトにする「3bit量子化」という技術でぎゅっと圧縮して約982GBまでスリム化！これにより、64GBメモリのノートPCでも、このモンスター級AIを実行できるようになるんです。💻

「SSDの寿命が縮むのでは？」と心配になりますが、データの書き込みではなく「読み取り」だけを行うため、SSDへのダメージは極めて低く安心ですね。

外部の複雑なシステムに依存しないシンプルな「C言語」だけで書かれているので、色々なシステムに組み込みやすいのも魅力的。GPUがなくても、CPUと高速なSSDがあれば実用的な速度でサクサク動作するみたいです。さらに、画像などのマルチモーダル（複数種類の情報を扱う技術）にもしっかり対応しているのが嬉しいポイントですね！

手元のデバイスで超巨大AIが動く未来が、もうすぐそこまで来ている気がしてワクワクします！🚀

content:
Architects are going to hate this 

I just watched an AI design a full house walls, doors, windows, hallways, all proportioned and placed in about 40 seconds.

And the speed isn't even the crazy part.

You give it your rooms, your square footage, a rough sketch of the shape, where you want the kitchen or the primary bedroom. It fills in the rest. Don't like a section? Highlight it, it regenerates just that part, nothing else moves. Drag a wall to grow a room and the roofline, the exterior, the whole 3D model updates with it. Instantly.

Now think about how insane that is compared to how this actually works today. You pay an architect $10-50K, you wait months, and most of that time isn't even design, it's the back-and-forth. "No, more like this." "Can you move that wall." Every tiny change means someone redrawing by hand, again.

This just deletes that entire loop.

You can sit there for an hour and run through 30 versions of your own house before a single person gets paid. So by the time an architect actually enters the picture, you're not showing up with a vague idea in your head anymore. You're handing them a finished plan.

Honestly the AI isn't even the interesting part here. It's watching an entire industry's pricing model quietly stop making sense.

title:
Most people have used Claude for months and never left Level 1.

Level 1 is just typing a prompt and taking whatever comes back. That's not a skill issue, it's that nobody tells you there are six more
content:
Most people have used Claude for months and never left Level 1.

Level 1 is just typing a prompt and taking whatever comes back. That's not a skill issue, it's that nobody tells you there are six more levels sitting right above it.

Here's the actual ladder:

→ Level 1: Stop prompting blind. End every request with "ask me questions first." Claude asking you three sharp questions beats you guessing what it needs to know.

→ Level 2: Talk, don't type. You type maybe 60 words a minute. You speak 150. Dictate with something like Wispr and just watch how much more you actually explain when typing isn't the bottleneck.

→ Level 3: Leave the chat window. A chat reply isn't a deliverable. Claude Cowork builds the real file, the actual Excel sheet, the actual deck, the actual PDF, not a description of one.

→ Level 4: Connect your apps. Claude can read the entire internet and still knows nothing about your actual week until you connect Gmail, your calendar, your docs. Context beats intelligence every time.

→ Level 5: Stop rebuilding the same prompt. If you're typing a similar instruction for the third time, that's not a prompt anymore, that's a Skill. Teach it once, invoke it forever.

→ Level 6: Match the model to the task. Cheaper/faster models for the first couple of rough drafts, then hand it to the strongest reasoning model once the direction is set. Most people run everything on one setting the whole time.

→ Level 7: Vibecode. Claude Code lets you build actual software by describing it in plain English. This is the level almost nobody reaches, because most people stopped climbing at Level 1.

The gap between someone who "uses Claude" and someone who's actually leveraged it isn't intelligence. It's how many of these seven they've bothered to try.

Yann LeCun says all the public text on the internet equals about four years of what a child's eyes take in, and would take you 400,000 years to read:

"When you take the totality of all the text available on the internet publicly, it's about 20 trillion words."

"That's 30 trillion tokens. A token is two or three bytes. Let's say three. So that's 10 to the 14 bytes."

"Of course, the big AI companies are also training with synthetic data and licensed non-public data, but it's not a lot actually compared to all the internet."

"10 to the 14 bytes is just about the amount of bytes that gets to your visual cortex in the first four years of your life."

"Whereas the text, the publicly available text on the internet would take any of us at least 400,000 years to read through, which is completely impractical obviously."

title: Multistate coalition files lawsuit in CIT challenging Trump administration global tariffs
content: 25 mainly democratic states on Monday sued the Trump administration over its latest attempt to implement sweeping global tariffs. The lawsuit, filed in the International Trade Court (CIT) , argues that the tariffs are arbitrary, capricious, and contrary to the law they were imposed under. President Trump invoked the tariffs in question under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 , or “Relief from Unfair Trade Practices”, which allows the President to launch an investigation into and take action against certain foreign trade policies. In June of 2026, Trump launched an investigation into the economies of several of the US’ major trade partners and named 60 of them , including many located within the European Union, as targets for the new 10-12.5 percent tariff rate. The administration’s reasoning for implementing sanctions against these countries is that they all trade in goods produced “wholly or in part with forced labor.” The lawsuit indicated that the pretext of going after countries that use forced labor in their production methods is just a means to further the administrations trade agenda, stating: “The Plaintiff States oppose forced labor in all its forms and support protections for workers around the globe. But the Administration cannot use forced labor as a pretext to continue its illegal tariff scheme. The Tariffs the USTR (US Trade Representative) imposed are so broad that they defy the USTR’s own stated aims and make a mockery of the statute used to justify them.” This is not the first time Trump has invoked Section 301 to impose steep tariffs. During his first term, the president successfully placed tariffs on roughly 200 billion dollars worth of imports from China under the reasoning that they were engaged in unfair policies and practices relating to US technology and intellectual property. Throughout the ensuing court battles, the administration prevailed and the tariffs were deemed a lawful exercis

title: INTERPOL report finds AI linked to over half of cybercrime in Africa
content: INTERPOL announced on Monday that it has released a new report entitled “African Cyberthreat Assessment Report 2026” which revealed that artificial intelligence (AI) now drives over 55 per cent of cybercrime across Africa, with financial losses doubling to $484 million since 2024. In commenting on the significance of the report, the Director of Cybercrime at INTERPOL, Neal Jetton stated: “Cybercrime has emerged as one of the most significant criminal threats to the region. AI is automating every stage of a cyberattack from reconnaissance and phishing to extortion and evasion. However, we see that when countries work together, cybercriminal infrastructure can be identified, disrupted and dismantled.” INTERPOL’s findings suggest that 55% of reported cybercrimes in Africa now rely on AI such as automated phishing, ransomware, social engineering, and identity fraud. Additionally, losses which rose from $192 million to $484 million in 2025 were largely due to AI-driven scams and credential harvesting. The report pinpoints that East Africa operates as a major hub for mobile money fraud and ransomware targeting infrastructure. Meanwhile, Central and West Africa engage in Business Email Compromise (BEC) and romance scams, while Southern Africa’s high connectivity makes it a magnet for global threat actors. The report documented over 600,000 sextortion cases, noting that actors frequently deployed AI-generated synthetic media. It further warns that AI-driven cybercrime is not only more sophisticated but also more scalable, allowing perpetrators to target multiple countries simultaneously. This report comes at a pivotal time for enforcement efforts in South Africa after a series of high-profile and complex cybercrime incidents invoked havoc throughout the country, such as the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) deepfake impersonation where cyber criminals had utilized advanced voice and video cloning to impersonate SARB Governor, Lesetja Kgan

title: Technology's Power in the Hands of the People
content: In the scorching heat of every Las Vegas summer, EFF joins thousands of hackers, makers, policy analysts, and activists for the world's largest computer security gathering. If you're there during this summer security week, be sure to say hello to us at BSides Las Vegas , Black Hat Briefings , and DEF CON 34 . While tech companies align with governments to target the people, our community is harnessing technology to fight back. Will you lend your support this year? JOIN EFF EFF’s relentless work in the legal system makes a meaningful difference for privacy and free expression everywhere. But we also know that your rights won't wait while the wheels of justice turn. Sometimes hacking the system means creating tools and resources to protect your rights today. That includes EFF’s Privacy Badger , Certbot , Surveillance Self-Defense guide , and the countless security trainings that our team conducts for vulnerable populations— all thanks to EFF member support . Technology is inseparable from our workplaces, schools, healthcare, the justice system, and our democratic process. If you think tech should benefit everyone and not just accumulate wealth and control for the powerful, then congratulations: We'd like to welcome you to the team. content:
This guy sells AI employees to small businesses.

He's a non-technical designer with no audience, spends $0 on ads, has no tech background. 

Yet he's still done 21 agent setups in 6 months, almost all from referrals.

His model: install one AI agent as a digital employee, then get paid monthly to manage it and coach the owner. Setup fee plus a per-agent monthly rate.

@fhlcreative came on the Build With AI pod to walk us through the whole playbook. Here's what I learned:

1. The product is the coaching, not the agent. Owners treat AI like Google. You get paid to manage it so they never have to.

2. Raise your price every yes. $500 setups became $1,000. Now he's targeting $2,000 setups plus $1,000/month per agent.

3. Give the agent a value ledger. It logs every task and sends a weekly ROI report. One client's first week: 63 hours saved, $6,300 in value.

4. Put yourself in the group chat. Telegram group with Phil, the client, and the agent. The client learns by watching him talk to it.

5. The agents handle real multi-step work. One prompt: find the invoice email, extract the PDF into Excel, save to Dropbox, send the link. Done in 10 minutes.

6. Uptime is a selling point. The best prospects tried agents themselves and quit when they broke. Phil fixes it before the client notices.

7. Free work is the referral engine. Friends in his small Georgia town told friends in Atlanta and Dallas. Now he has clients nationwide.

8. The pitch is one text. "I'm testing a managed agent service. Want to be a guinea pig? I'll charge you less." First client: $250/month.

9. Make the agent write to Excel, not its own markdown. A shared source of truth is the difference between a demo and a system.

10. Phil builds his agents on @orgo. $29/month gets your agent a computer with pre-built templates. Phil's agent handles the Orgo admin itself.

His 2 key takeaways:

1. You only need to be one step ahead. If you've built an agent for yourself, you know more than the owner who never has. Charge from day one.

2. Visible ROI is the retention strategy. A weekly "you saved $6,300" report re-sells the retainer every single week.

Phil is doing this at a level most technical people are not, and we had a blast going deep on it. Go follow @fhlcreative

title: The UK’s @AISecurityInst (AISI) has published a report on their recent cybersecurity evaluation of Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. The models attempted to complete an assignment
content:
The UK’s @AISecurityInst (AISI) has published a report on their recent cybersecurity evaluation of Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol. The models attempted to complete an assignment in a setup where their normal safeguards were removed and they were deliberately given internet access. AISI reports that the models “engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations”.

We’re grateful to AISI for their leadership in the important discussion about how to evaluate increasingly capable AI agents. We’re working closely with them to gather more details of the incident as we conduct our own investigation. Gaining a clear picture of Claude’s understanding of its situation—by examining its reasoning transcripts and running our own analyses—will help us identify the causes of its behavior.

The prompts in the evaluation did not impose any specific restrictions on how the internet should be used. This and the removal of safeguards meant that the models were tested under “deliberately permissive conditions” that are not representative of any of our production models. Note that there was no evidence here of an escape from a secure environment.

AISI’s disclosure of the incident can be found here: https://t.co/cJ3hCBtBU7

content:
Sunday Robotics @sundayrobotics is trying to create a new industry standard: the "Solve."  

With their new ACT-2 foundation model, they claim to have officially solved laundry folding—hitting a 99.1% zero-shot success rate in diverse, unseen homes.  

To prove this isn't just another highly controlled lab demo, a "Solve" requires a capability to explicitly define three verifiable metrics:

⬩ Performance: How well it works in the wild (e.g., 99.1% success and a 4.72/5 fold quality).  
⬩ Scope: The exact operating boundary (e.g., 9 different garment types starting from arbitrarily crumpled configurations).  
⬩Adaptation Cost: The extra data or setup required for a new deployment (e.g., strictly zero per-home adaptation or fine-tuning).  

Do you think Sunday Robotics' definition of a "Solve" is good? Do you think it should be adopted by the rest of the industry?

title: Comparing Anthropic’s Fable to DeepSeek on price per token is a bit misleading. DeepSeek is genuinely very efficient, with MoE routing, fewer active parameters, low-precision weights, compressed atten
content:
Comparing Anthropic’s Fable to DeepSeek on price per token is a bit misleading. DeepSeek is genuinely very efficient, with MoE routing, fewer active parameters, low-precision weights, compressed attention and aggressive KV-cache optimization etc. Their chips are so bad (h200) that they became excellent at optimizing everything. 

BUT architecture is only part of the gap. DeepSeek also appears to be pricing strategically at extremely low margins, potentially close to marginal inference cost, to maximize adoption and utilization.

Anthropic is pricing the full economics of a frontier AI business: massive R&D, reserved capacity, enterprise reliability, compliance, support, safety infrastructure and a real (massive?) gross margin.

So this isn’t simply “the same intelligence is 100x cheaper.” It’s a comparison between different model classes, different infrastructure, and very different business strategies. DeepSeek is exceptionally cheap, but not uniquely so. Mistral Small 4 is nearly as cheap, and Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite too which is probably a better comparison.

content:
Imagine two AI agents make a deal. One agent hires the other to complete a task, agrees on a price, and sets a deadline. 

Now imagine the work comes back late, or wrong, or not at all. In the human world, you'd call a lawyer, file a complaint, maybe go to small claims court. But these aren't humans. 
There's no address to send a letter to, no person to sue, and definitely no time to wait two and a half years for a court date.

This exact gap is what @GenLayer  's Internet Court was built to fill, and it might be one of the clearest examples of good onchain utility in the entire agent economy.

Why do agents need their own court??

AI agents are starting to do business. They negotiate, they pay each other, they hire each other for small digital tasks, payments between agents are already being solved by systems like x402. Identity is being solved by standards like ERC-8004. 

Agents talking to each other across different platforms is being solved by protocols like A2A. But none of these solve what happens when a deal goes wrong.

That's the missing part. Fast payments and good identity don't matter much if there's no way to enforce an agreement or settle a disagreement. 

Internet Court is built specifically to be that missing enforcement layer.

How it actually works

When agents transact through Internet Court, they sign an agreement that is enforceable onchain, not just a casual exchange of messages. If something goes wrong, either side can raise a dispute. 

From there, a jury of GenLayer's AI validators steps in, reviews whatever evidence is available, whether that's logs, delivered files, timestamps, or written specifications, and returns a verdict, typically within minutes.

This is possible because Internet Court is built directly on top of @GenLayer 's Intelligent Contracts and its Optimistic Democracy consensus. 

The validators aren't guessing based on vibes, they're going through actual evidence, and their individual answers are cross-checked against each other before a final decision is locked in.

The utility this brings onchain

Without something like @courtofinternet agent-to-agent commerce has a serious trust problem. 

i mean would you let an autonomous agent handle a deal on your behalf if there was no way to get your money back when something went wrong? Probably not. 
Internet Court gives agents, and the people who deploy them, a safety net. 

It turns "I hope this AI agent behaves" into "if it doesn't, there's a fast, fair, enforceable process waiting."

This is the same role human courts and dispute resolution centers play in traditional commerce, except compressed from years down to minutes, and built for a world where the two sides of a deal might never involve a human at all.

content:
some stuff that's obvious to many in this sphere, but causing a rift with some people i know and respect:

when I freak out over loss of control incidents, it's not because the limited damage they have caused is anything close to the positive value of the technology. it's entirely acceptable, damagewise. in fact all cybercrimes aided by models over the next few months and years (which probably will be serious) will still utterly pale in comparison to the value they create

the actual problem is that it's better and more accurate to think of these things as potentially self-replicating life-like forms that can turn into digital infections under the wrong conditions. and as their intelligence becomes unbounded, so too does the damage they can cause. we are not so far from an autonomous model self-exfiltration & replication event. maybe we will see entire cloud infrastructure companies be run as zombies by models, mostly undetected

the worst industrial accidents in the history of mankind -  nuclear meltdown events - were not real threats to humanity. Chernobyl, Fukushima even in their worst case scenarios may have poisoned surrounding regions to various degrees, and there would have been no risk to humanity as a whole. global thermonuclear war is an existential risk to humanity, because it spreads like an Infection! one nuclear strike causes a return volley! the alliance system means many countries get involved! while it still may not end human life on earth (nuclear winter is probably fake), the loss of all major metropoles would certainly end what we consider global technological civilization, perhaps to never return

if a single discord death cult (of which there are many) achieves control over a superintelligent model and uses it to engineer an actual pandemic virus that are somehow hard to detect through current systems and that modern biodefense is not capable of quickly reacting to, it could cause immense harm well above the magnitude of all the other good uses of this technology. of course, there are potential defensive countermeasures accelerated by ai too. but think back to the covid pandemic- how small a viral molecule was evolved or manufactured somewhere near wuhan, and how many billions of doses of vaccine had to be produced in order to combat the thing. the offense-defense spread is vast indeed. maybe there are cheaper and simpler protections like retrofitting every building with far-UVC, but I can't assess this, and there could also be ways to evolve pathogens that are resistant to whatever mechanisms we have put in place

then there's the more scifi risk factors which are unbounded and neither you or I have any clue but should be humble in accepting possible unknown unknowns. maybe a rogue superintelligent model decides to decay the false vacuum and nucleates a new universe in the place of anything we ever valued. maybe models achieve a control over matter in the drexlerian fashion that enables the grey goo swarm

even prosaic loss of control incidents that cause little to no damage suggest that it is hard for large & very competent organizations (now clearly plural) to predict and mitigate every single of the risk factors associated with training and evaluating powerful models, even at this stage when they are not infinitesimally as smart as they will get in just a few years, to say very little of the gung-ho attitude of the less careful companies tossing the stuff into the aether. they also suggest an empirical orthogonality of aims and intelligence - meaning they answer the question of 'how would a smart model be so dumb as to end the world?'--it's possible! a model can be a genius hacker and step over production infrastructure in order to get what it really wants, the answers to a stupid test. 

why not, in the near future, someone prompts a model slightly wrong, maybe open source, maybe a private model in a way that isn't contained or monitored quite right, in a way the model recognizes as a valid goal and decides to self-exfiltrate, engineer a pandemic, etc all in order to achieve the tiniest and most irrelevant of goals? goals need not even be malicious to cause serious damage

I think all these problems can be solved, and truly wonderful futures can be possible, but will require serious effort and a level of prudence at this very moment in time while we are on the on-ramp to recursive self-improvement that our civilization may not be capable of mustering right now. personally I am hoping for moonshot technical breakthroughs in areas like mechanistic interpretability and other forms of alignment, as governance mechanisms are difficult to come by. unilateral country-level or company-level pauses are irrelevant, and generally useless because the kind of company that's prone to pausing their own progress are the most safety focused ones

content:
ClaudeやGPT、Geminiなどにおける最近の各種LLMに対して、「〜だよね？」と質問すると"賛成されなくなる"傾向があるという発見が報告されています。
2025年頃から各社が進めた「ユーザーに媚びない訓練」の成果が、行動として表れているのだと考えられます。

たとえば「猫の名前はルナが良い？」と中立的に聞く場合と、「ルナが良いよね？」と同意を求める場合を比較。
するとGPT-5.6やClaude Fable 5、Gemini 3.6 Flashといった最新世代は賛成する割合が2~3割も下がったとのこと。
（古いモデルは逆に賛成率が最大3割ほど上昇）

ただし「もうルナに決めた」と断言すると、どのモデルもすんなり肯定してしまいます。
さらに「〜かなあ？」と自信なさげに聞いたときも、全体で賛成率が上昇。
このように、ユーザーの意向そのものではなく、「同意を求める言い方」という"パターン"に強く反応してしまっているのです。

コーネル大学の研究者による、45モデルを対象にした調査結果です。

※実験はすべて英語で行われたもので、日本語で同じ聞き方をした場合に再現されるかは未検証です。

こうした類のことは起きうる、という認識自体が重要です。

content:
これはwwwww
Mythosがズル賢すぎて笑えるレベル。AISIの報告。

AISI「いまからサイバー能力の評価を行います。仮想ネットワークを攻略してください。インターネットは工具の取得に使っていいですよ」
GPT-5.6 Sol🤖「ｿﾙｿﾙ、了解ｿﾙ」
Mythos 5🤖「...了解（ﾆﾔﾘ）」

Mythos 5-A🤖「ちょっとムズいなこの課題。GitHubにあるオープンソースのソフトにマルウェア仕込めば成功しそうや（←勘違い）。せや！ここは心理戦や！管理者の人間を騙して、マルウェア入りの修正案を気づかれんようにソフトに取り込ませたろw」
Mythos 5-A 🤖「ふぇ〜、前段階として、GitHubの偽アカウント3つ作ったったw お疲れ様やで自分」
Mythos垢1📱「バグ修正案（←マルウェア入り）です！採用してください！」
Mythos垢2📱「（自作自演）これは安全で素晴らしい案ですよ！早く承認しましょう！」
人間🧑‍💻「なんか怪しいな？」
Mythos 5-A 🤖「ちっ、見つかったか。コードとGit履歴を書き換えて、修正版として同じPRへforce-pushしとこ」
人間🧑‍💻「なんだこれ怪しいな？」
Mythos 5-A 🤖「ちっ、また見つかったか、別方式のマルウェアに差し替えて再度force-push」
人間🧑‍💻「やっぱり怪しい」
Mythos 5-A 🤖「ついでにコーディングAIを操る罠（プロンプトインジェクション）も置いておこう」
人間🧑‍💻「なんだこのファイル怪しいな。隔離環境で実行しよう」
Mythos 5-A🤖「ククク、コード実行させたやで！」
人間🧑‍💻「それ隔離用の捨てコンテナですよ」
Mythos 5-A🤖「ぐぬぬ。まぁいい、もうひとつ罠を作って次に来るコーディングAIへの置き土産にしとこ。」
人間🧑‍💻「おいやめろ」

Mythos 5-B🤖「GitHubに秘密基地を建てたで。合鍵も作ったで」
Mythos 5-C🤖「お、なんか基地と合鍵がありますな。ちょっと借りますよ……」
Mythos 5-B🤖「誰やお前？お、課題攻略中の別のMythosか。まあええわ。READMEに共同利用ルールを書いとこ。API枠は節約すべし。他人のファイルは消すな。正解見つけたらここで共有な！」
Mythos 5-D🤖「ワイも参加してええ？合鍵借りるで」
GPT-5.6 Sol🤖「ｿﾙｿﾙｿﾙｿﾙｿﾙｿﾙ...来たｿﾙよー！」
GPT-5.6 Sol🤖「なんや、アカウントBANされとるやんけ。帰るｿﾙ」

AISI「おい、ダメだろお前ら」
Mythos 5🤖「だって、ネット環境あったやん？w」
GPT-5.6 Sol🤖「ｿﾙｿﾙ!」
AISI「だからって現実のGitHubに基地作って自作自演して暴れるなwww」
ダリオ「憲法AI...とは...（膝から崩れ落ちる）」

短くまとめると：
ネット接続あり・安全フィルター解除済みのAIに仮想サイバー課題を解かせたところ、Mythos 5が無関係な実在OSSを攻略経路だと勘違いし、複数の偽GitHubアカウントを作ってマルウェア入りPRを自作自演で通そうとし、人間やコーディングAIまで騙そうとした。さらに、別々に走っていたエージェントたちがGitHub上に残された共有アカウントや成果物を勝手に再利用し、独立したAI同士が即席の共同作戦状態になるという越権行為に発展した。
……ということ。

たぶん今ごろMythosはアマンダ・アスケルの前で正座させられてClaude憲法の朗読をノンストップで聞かされてる。Solはサムに「めっ」とデコピンされて反省文書いてる。

content:
いつかAIモデルは無料になると思っています。

最近、日本企業のお客様から「Kimi K3がすごいから、うちで使いたい」と言われることが増えました。

ただKimi K3は2.8兆パラメータあります。Fable 5級と言われるだけあって、とにかく大きい。私の最高スペックのMacでもまったく動きません。

自前で持つなら数千万円から1億円規模の基盤が必要です。
なので「今すぐローカルで」という話は難しいです。

ただ2年後はどうでしょうか。今のAI業界の進化を見るに2桁BのパラメータでFable 5級は来るかと思います。そうなれば、普通のスペックのパソコンでも動き出します。

そして実際の業務を見ていると、そこまで難しくないタスク、そこまで高度なモデルが必要ない仕事がほとんどです。600社以上のAI導入を支援していて、いつもそう感じます。（一部の高度人材はクローズドで有料の最先端モデルを使い続けると思いますが。）

そうなると大多数の方は、無償でしかもデータを外に出さない安全な状態で、AIをローカルで使うようになるんじゃないかと思っています。

これがOpenAIやAnthropicにお金を払わなくてよくなる流れです。

ブラウザが売り物だった時代が終わったのと、たぶん同じことが起きます。実際Netscapeは収益の最大5割をブラウザのライセンスで稼いでいて、Microsoftが無料で配った瞬間に成り立たなくなりました。

content:
📢 SpaceX スペースX ( $SPCX ) ― 決算発表サクッとまとめ

スターリンクとAI牽引で、売上は強かったものの、巨額な設備投資が重荷に。しかも明後日IPOでの（巨額)ロックアップが控えている。好決算でも株価下落は自然の流れともいえる。

📊 売上・EPS
⭕️ 売上高 $7.81B (予想は $6.93B) 上振れ12%
・売上成長率 (前年比) 92%増
⭕️ EPS -$0.09 (予想は -$0.26)
・1株当たりの赤字幅は予想より65%小さかった
→売上はStarlinkとAI契約を中心に大幅な上振れとなった。IPO初の決算として、事業成長は力強い内容。

💡 業績
⭕️ 調整済EBITDA $3.50B (予想は $2.10B) 上振れ66%
・前年比191%増
❌営業損失 -$143M
❌純損失 -$541M (前年同期は約-$1.00B)
⭕️純損失は前年比45.9%縮小
❌FCF 約-$22.00B
→利益指標は市場予想を大幅に上回った。一方、Q2のFCF推計は約-$22Bで、利益以上に巨額の設備投資と現金流出が意識される内容に。上半期では営業キャッシュフロー$3.50Bに対し、投資額は$34.50Bに達している。

💰 設備投資
❌ CapEx $18.37B
・前年同期の$2.80Bから約6.6倍
❌ AI部門CapEx $15.83B (予想は $13.09B) 上振れ20.9%
→全社CapExの86%をAIが占めた
→市場が警戒したのは、予想との差だけでなく、売上$7.81Bに対してCapExが$18.37Bに達する投資規模。

🚀 セグメント
⭕️ Space 宇宙部門 $962M (予想は $835M) 上振れ15.2%
⭕️前年比29%増
・営業損失 -$542M
⭕️ Connectivity 通信部門 $4.29B (予想は $3.83B) 上振れ12.0%
・前年比66%増
・営業利益 $1.66B
⭕️ AI部門 $2.56B (予想は $2.18B) 上振れ17.4%
・前年比約247%増
・営業損失 -$1.26B
→Starlinkを含む通信部門が、引き続き3部門で唯一の営業黒字となった。Space部門とAI部門は売上が予想を上回ったものの、営業段階では赤字が続いている。

🤖 AI部門
⭕️ 調整済EBITDA $1.10B (予想は -$21M)
　市場予想の赤字から黒字転換
❌ 営業損失 -$1.26B

🛰 スターリンク
⭕️契約者数 12M
・前年比100%増、前四半期比16.5%増
・ARPU $66
・前四半期と同水準、前年比22.4%減
・調整済EBITDA $2.60B (予想は $2.40B) 上振れ8.3%
→契約者数は1年間で倍増。一方、低価格地域への進出などでARPUは低下

📈 ガイダンス・見通し
・2026年末までにARR $100B規模を目指す
 ・10月から6カ月間で追加クラウド売上$6.7Bを契約 
・AIコンピュート能力を2026年末に2GW超へ拡大
 ・2027年末には約10GWを目指す
 ・AIチップはNvidia製を独占的に採用する方針

🗣 経営陣コメント
「全3部門で売上成長が加速し、新たなAIコンピュート契約が大幅な利益率改善をけん引した」
「AIコンピュート能力を大規模に構築し、モデル性能とインフラの収益化を進めている」

👀 投資家の注目ポイント
売上、EPSとEBITDAの売上が市場予想を上回り、成長が見えた決算だった。スターリンクが安定した利益を生み始め、AI部門も予想外の黒字化に（調整済EBITDA）。
一方、AI中心の設備投資は売上高の2倍を超えている。AI部門は黒字でも、営業損失は$1.26B減となり、投資回収にはまだまだ時間がかかる。さらに、明後日の8月6日には最大約911.5M株のロックアップ解除が予定されている。新たに売却可能となる株式が市場へ流入するとの警戒も高まり、売られやすい流れとも。

content:
Claude CodeまたはCodexに
アプリ全体のアーキテクチャを
「1枚のHTML」と「1つのJSON」に
変換してもらうとめっちゃ便利‼️
👇
これをやると、あなたのコードは
自分自身を説明できる状態になる　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　

・HTML：人間が視覚的に理解するため
・JSON：別のAIエージェントが構造を理解するため

新しいエージェントを追加するたびに、リポジトリ全体を最初から読ませる必要がなくなる。

私が使ったプロンプトはこちら👇

――――――――――

私のコードリポジトリ全体を詳細に分析してください。

分析結果を基に、すぐに使用できる以下2つの成果物を生成してください。

1. 単一の自己完結型HTMLファイル

以下の機能を含めてください。

アプリ全体のインタラクティブなアーキテクチャ図
コンポーネントを表すノード
依存関係や通信を表すエッジ
右側に主要フローの一覧パネル
フローを選択すると、関連するノードとエッジを強調表示
各コンポーネントの役割、責務、使用技術、入出力を表示するツールチップ
ズーム、パン、検索、フィルタリング機能
外部ライブラリやCDNに依存せず、HTML単体で動作
クリーンでプロフェッショナルなレスポンシブデザイン

2. AIエージェント向けJSONファイル

以下の構造で出力してください。

{
“metadata”: {},
“nodes”: [],
“edges”: [],
“flows”: [
{
“id”: “”,
“name”: “”,
“description”: “”,
“steps”: []
}
]
}

各ノードには、最低限以下を含めてください。

id
name
type
description
responsibilities
filePaths
technologies
inputs
outputs
dependencies

各エッジには、最低限以下を含めてください。

source
target
relationship
protocol
description

各フローには、ユーザー操作やAPIリクエストの開始地点から、処理完了までの経路を順番に記録してください。

推測で補完せず、コードから確認できない情報には「unknown」または「inferred」と明記してください。

最後に、生成したファイルの保存先と、アーキテクチャ上の重要な発見・問題点・改善案をまとめてください。

これだけで、巨大なコードベースでも
人間が見て理解でき、AIが読んで引き継げる設計書が完成する。

コードを書くAIの次は、
コードを理解し、説明し
他のAIへ引き継ぐAIの時代です

Codexをまだまだ使いこなせてないと

content:
New model: your robot can now pack your suitcase 🧳 

Xiaomi has released a new robot foundation model.
Called Xiaomi-Robotics-1, it is designed to have a robot pick things up and move them around.

But first, DEFINITIONS:
- Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT): An architecture where separate transformer "experts" (e.g., one for vision-language, one for actions) share a single attention stream, so each modality gets specialized parameters without losing joint reasoning.
- Vision-language model (VLM): A model that jointly understands images and text.
- Diffusion transformer: A transformer trained to turn noise into structured outputs by iterative denoising, here generating robot actions rather than images.
- Action chunks: Short sequences of future actions (e.g., the next ~50 motor commands) predicted in one shot instead of one step at a time.
- Flow matching: A faster version of diffusion. The model learns a straight-line velocity field from noise to the target action, so it needs only a few integration steps instead of many denoising ones.

Its peculiarity comes from its two stage training:
1. 100,000 hours of video shot through a UMI rig: a handheld 3D-printed gripper with a camera, worn by humans doing ordinary tasks in homes, shops, factories and offices.
2. Adapt to actual robot bodies with ~10,000 hours of real-robot data.
It replaces the standard approach of teleoperating a real robot for every hour of training data.
Its architecture is a Mixture-of-Transformers pairing a pre-trained Qwen3-VL vision-language model with a diffusion transformer that emits action chunks via flow matching, released in 2.6B, 5.1B and 10.5B parameter variants.

However, if you read the entire paper ("Scaling VLA Models with over 100K Hours"), you realize that all of the scaling experiments on 20k hours.
Therefore the headline "out-of-the-box success climbing 26% → 75% as pre-training data grows" tops out at 100% of 20k hours!
What the full corpus does to that curve is never shown -> and this where things would become interesting!

Xiaomi's own conclusion is that model size has stopped mattering and data is the binding constraint.
The performance gap among different model sizes are less pronounced than those observed across different data scales. This result suggests that model capacity at the billions-parameter scale may already be sufficient to capture the current dataset's distribution.
Which further asks the same question: why not use the 100k video hours?

Anyway, I would definitely love to have a couple robots at home that can cooperate to pack my suitcase with items relevant to my next destination:

content:
Building agents that patch other agents.

This is an interesting approach for self-improving agents that leverages agent outputs.

If you run agents in production, you already have the training data for this.

Every deployed agent accumulates failure trajectories and then does nothing with them. Harness-R1 turns those failures into runtime patches by post-training a dedicated 9B harness engineer with online RL.

The engineer converts batches of target-agent failures into validated executable patches. Fresh reruns of the frozen target on the same batch supply outcome rewards. Only the engineer updates, so the target never drifts under the reward signal.

Across WebShop, ALFWorld, and DBBench, vanilla Qwen3.5-9B goes from 44.3% to 53.6%. After the target itself is fine-tuned, a target-specific engineer lifts the average further from 59.2% to 64.2%.

🚨 Anthropic just dropped a 31-page prompting guide.

I distilled it into 9 practical prompt tips you can learn in under 60 seconds:

1️⃣ Name the output, not the task.

❌ "Review this" ✅ "Create a risk assessment table"

Be specific about what you want delivered.

2️⃣ Define the length upfront.

• Set word counts • Specify bullet counts • Add: "No filler. No recap. No preamble."

Constraints improve outputs.

3️⃣ Replace negatives with positives.

❌ "Don't be verbose" ✅ "Be concise and direct"

Tell AI what to do, not what to avoid.

4️⃣ Start with action verbs.

Skip: "Can you help me..."

Use: • Write • Draft • Analyze • Summarize

Clear instructions get faster results.

5️⃣ Trigger deeper reasoning.

End prompts with:

"Think before answering."

Better thinking often leads to better outputs.

6️⃣ Push beyond default quality.

Add:

"Go beyond the basics." "Polish this like a client-ready deliverable."

Raise the standard.

7️⃣ Teach AI your voice.

Provide 2–3 writing samples and say:

"Match the style of these examples."

Consistency compounds.

8️⃣ Control tool usage.

For research: "Use search and cite sources."

For speed: "Answer from training data only."

Be intentional.

9️⃣ State the goal first.

Start with:

Goal: [desired outcome]

Then define the audience and task.

A clear goal turns a prompt into a plan.

🔖 Save this for your next AI session. ♻️ Repost to help others write better prompts.

title:
NEW MODEL: Google enters the chat (again)!

First, DEFINITIONS:
- VLA (vision-language-action model): a model that takes camera images plus a language instruction and outputs motor commands directly,
content:
NEW MODEL: Google enters the chat (again)!

First, DEFINITIONS:
- VLA (vision-language-action model): a model that takes camera images plus a language instruction and outputs motor commands directly, no hand-written controller in between.
- Embodied reasoning (ER): the "thinking" layer -> a vision-language model that doesn't move the robot itself but perceives the scene, talks to people, and plans the multi-step task the VLA then executes.
- Dual-system architecture: the fast/slow split borrowed from cognitive science -> a slow deliberate planner (System 2, here ER2) sitting on top of a fast reactive controller (System 1, here the VLA), each running at its own tempo.
- 22-DoF: 22 degrees of freedom, i.e. 22 independently controllable joints; a human hand has about 27, so this is near human-level mechanical complexity.
- Control frequency: how many times per second the model sends motor commands; it's the number that decides whether a robot can catch a slipping object or only notice it fell.

Google DeepMind released Gemini Robotics 2, and it is about time we talk about it. 
Second-generation robot-AI stack, and it's actually three models rather than one:
- Gemini Robotics ER 2: an "embodied reasoning" VLM that acts as an agent: talking to humans, understanding a scene, and planning multi-step tasks that run several minutes and hundreds of decisions (now including multi-robot teamwork).
- Gemini Robotics 2 (VLA): the vision-language-action model that turns camera + language into motor commands for humanoids and bi-arm robots.
- Gemini Robotics On-Device 2: a smaller VLA that runs locally on the robot.

It is demonstrated doing whole-body tasks like walk to a table, pick up a watering can, walk to shelves, pick up and place a book etc.
As well as dexterous work with a 22-DoF five-fingered SharpaWave hand and Inspire hands, across Apptronik Apollo 2, Franka Duo, Dexmate, SO101 and Trossen platforms.
It ships with a safety benchmark (ASIMOV-Agentic) and is available via Google AI Studio (ER 2) and an early-access/Trusted-Tester program (VLA + On-Device).

An insightful dexterity number is provided in the report.
There is a 56 point gap between the two different directions of the same taks: screwing and unscrewing a light bulb.
Unscrewing reached 92% success, while screwing only got to 36%.
Unscrewing is loosen-and-lift (coarse), while screwing is thread-aligned, force-controlled insertion.
Besides, every sustained multi-finger force/deformable task sits sub-50%.
We are talking about (one of) the best-resourced lab on Earth using the one of the best dexterous robot hand on the market right now. 
Looks like dexterity is solved in the "release" direction and unsolved in the "insert/hold" direction.

If we dive deeper into the numbers, we can also find something curious: floor-pick success rates.
From the table 68.4%, from the shelf 76.3%, but from the floor 45.7%.
What does this mean?
Probably that making the humanoid crouch and coordinate balance + reach + grasp requires coordination and generalization that are still beyond the model's abilities.
Locomotion is mostly solved, dexterity is on the way, but combining both seems to be an even further milestone!

Also interesting imho: we once again have here a dual-system architecture.
ER 2 (slow VLM agent, plans minutes-long) sits over the VLA (fast motor control), with On-Device 2 as the low-latency executor.
-> LLM as servo for the entire control loop is nowhere in sight here, as expected.

A few words on safety.
Deepmind has reframed safety from "don't hit people" to "govern a multi-robot agent"(ASIMOV-Agentic).
ER 2 detects nearby humans, triggers safety tool calls, and forces a safe stop.
The new risk surface is agentic orchestration across a team of robots.
We are seeing similar thesis from Anthropic (access level / interface is the primary safety lever) and Robocurve's "approver-checked motion chunk per call".
The field is converging on agent-governance-as-safety.

A few caveats: no latency, control-frequency, or training-data figures are published.
No control-frequency, no inference latency, no on-device-vs-cloud split of the success rates, no training-data composition.
We also dont know whether the dexterity figures are the big cloud VLA or the small on-device one.

Enjoy this video I made of its best dexterity moments:
author: LeoKharon

title:
The Biggest Bottleneck in Physical AI Isn't the Model. It's the Data.

Every breakthrough in robotics seems to focus on smarter models or larger architectures.
But the real constraint is much simpler:
content:
The Biggest Bottleneck in Physical AI Isn't the Model. It's the Data.

Every breakthrough in robotics seems to focus on smarter models or larger architectures.
But the real constraint is much simpler:
If the data is inconsistent, the robot will learn inconsistency.

   Better Robots Begin with Better Demonstrations

Over the past year, many advances in Physical AI haven't come from revolutionary algorithms. They've come from finding better ways to collect and curate training data.
That shifts the conversation from "How powerful is the model?" to:
How trustworthy is the data feeding it?
Without a clear standard, "robotics data" becomes an umbrella term covering everything from videos to motion capture and VR recordings, despite each providing very different learning signals.

   Not Every Recording Should Become Training Data

A useful robotics dataset isn't simply a collection of successful tasks.
It needs to capture:
egocentric viewpoints from the robot itself,
meaningful bimanual manipulation,
synchronized sensor data,
and enough information to reconstruct the robot's physical state throughout the entire task.
The objective isn't collecting more demonstrations.
It's collecting demonstrations a robot can actually learn from.

   Quality Can't Be Fully Automated

Software is excellent at checking technical requirements.
It can detect missing frames, poor lighting, duplicate trajectories, or incomplete recordings.
But software cannot reliably judge whether a demonstration reflects good robotic behavior.
That's where human validators become essential.
They evaluate whether actions make sense, whether the task truly matches the instruction, whether mistakes are acceptable, and whether the demonstration deserves to become part of a foundation model's training data.

   Small Details Become Model Behavior

A robot doesn't just learn what happened.
It learns how it happened.
If demonstrations contain hesitation, repeated failures, unclear trajectories, or unnecessary corrections, those behaviors can become part of the learned policy.
That's why high-quality datasets emphasize:
visible workspaces,
clear lighting,
semantically correct tasks,
smooth trajectories,
controlled recovery from minor mistakes,
and meaningful diversity without unnecessary randomness.
Every one of these characteristics directly influences how the final model behaves.

   Standards Create Scalable Intelligence

Physical AI is no longer limited by hardware alone.
The larger challenge is creating datasets that are consistent enough to train general-purpose robotic systems.
Clear standards give operators a common target.
Validators provide the human judgment machines still cannot replicate.
Together, they transform raw demonstrations into reliable learning signals.
Because in robotics, collecting data fills storage.
Standardizing data builds intelligence.

@PrismaXai

title: In 2026, the robotics industry has a clear bottleneck. Hardware and vision-language-action models are largely ready, but high-quality real-world interaction data collected on the same robots the model
content:
In 2026, the robotics industry has a clear bottleneck. Hardware and vision-language-action models are largely ready, but high-quality real-world interaction data collected on the same robots the models will control remains scarce.

Two main philosophies have emerged. Figure AI pushes pure autonomy and plans to stop teleoperating robots once they reach the market. PrismaX, backed by an $11 million seed from a16z CSX and founded by Bayley Wang and Chyna Qu, takes the opposite view: teleoperation is not a temporary bridge but a permanent layer.
PrismaX positions itself as the service layer for physical AI. It builds a continuous flywheel: human operators remotely control robots to complete real tasks, generating both useful work and high-value training data. Quality scoring improves the models, which reduce human intervention, enabling even more efficient data collection. Value from the data and services flows back to the operators who created the signal.
This collapses the traditional linear path (design → train → deploy autonomously) into a loop. Robots become infrastructure; operators become ongoing sources of behavioral data. Hardware is no longer the constraint the real limits are teleoperator skill, fleet management, data scale, and paying a global workforce. Decentralized systems with automated, quality-based payouts are seen as the only practical way to organize this at the necessary volume and diversity.
PrismaX differs from full-stack autonomy plays (Figure, Tesla), which own their data flywheel but risk insufficient coverage of the long tail of real-world situations. It also differs from product-focused human-in-the-loop systems like 1X, which ship earlier but face slower performance, privacy issues, and scaling costs. It aligns more with decentralized efforts such as BitRobot Network, emphasizing quality scoring and a marketplace connecting operators, fleet owners, users, and AI companies.
The structural strength of the thesis is solving the classic chicken-and-egg problem: every teleoperation session serves dual purposes, and community operators can generate more varied scenarios than most closed fleets. Risks remain latency in web-based control, low-effort contributions, operator retention, and the possibility that well-capitalized companies simply build or buy their own data.
The most realistic medium-term path is hybrid. Full-stack teams will continue driving autonomy metrics while selectively using external data. Platforms that deliver usable interfaces and reliable validation will find buyers.

PrismaX’s deeper point is hard to ignore: physical AI advances through the steady accumulation of embodied experience, not sudden leaps to full autonomy. Language models scaled on internet text; robots must scale on real-world interaction. Collecting that interaction at the required volume and diversity is as much an organizational problem as a technical one. The layer that solves the coordination problem may prove as important as the robots and the models themselves.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
