title:
What would it take to give any atomistic method access to state-of-the-art van der Waals interactions?🧲 That's the idea behind MBD-ML, our new work published in PRX Intelligence! 

vdW interactions de
content:
What would it take to give any atomistic method access to state-of-the-art van der Waals interactions?🧲 That's the idea behind MBD-ML, our new work published in PRX Intelligence! 

vdW interactions determine how molecular crystals pack, how proteins fold, and how drugs bind. Yet they are still missing from many exchange-correlation functionals and most local ML force fields. Many-body dispersion (MBD) is one of the most accurate dispersion methods available, and it needs just atomic a0 polarizabilities and C6 coefficients as input. Until now, these quantities had to come from Hirshfeld partitioning of the DFT electron density, so every MBD calculation first required a full electronic-structure calculation.  

MBD-ML removes that dependency. It's a small pretrained message-passing neural network (trained on 33.5M structures from the QCML dataset) that predicts atomic a0 and C6 ratios directly from positions. These ratios are passed to libMBD, which builds and diagonalizes the coupled quantum Drude oscillator Hamiltonian to compute energies, forces, and stresses.

Against the MBD-NL reference, MBD-ML reproduces energies to <1 meV/atom, forces to <1 meV/Å and stresses to <0.2 meV/Å³. Pairwise dispersion corrections show ~10× larger force errors, reflecting the many-body nature of dispersion. For molecular crystals, relaxed cell volumes stay within 1% (see animation) and polymorph rankings within 0.6 kJ/mol per molecule. It also scales to ~13k atoms on a single 128-core node.

We highlight two main limitations: inorganic solids and systems with alkali/alkaline-earth elements are underrepresented in the training data, and molecular anions remain genuinely hard for electronic structure theory.

Anything that produces atomic positions, whether a DFT code, a semi-empirical method, an ML force field, or a generative model can now have MBD added on top (via one function call). See links below.

Huge thanks to my co-authors Evgeny Moerman (who led the work), Almaz Khabibrakhmanov, and Alexandre Tkatchenko (University of Luxembourg). Calculations were performed on MeluXina and funded by the European Research Council (ERC) and the Luxembourg National Research Fund (FNR).

title:
Elucidating enzyme–substrate specificity through co-folding foundation model

1 Boltz2ESI is presented as an end-to-end enzyme–substrate specificity predictor that replaces “pocket definition + rigid
content:
Elucidating enzyme–substrate specificity through co-folding foundation model

1 Boltz2ESI is presented as an end-to-end enzyme–substrate specificity predictor that replaces “pocket definition + rigid docking” with native enzyme–ligand co-folding, aiming to capture ligand-induced active-site plasticity directly from sequence + substrate SMILES.

2 The core idea is a two-stage structural protocol built on the Boltz-2 co-folding foundation model: (i) MSA-guided co-folding to localize a putative active site, then (ii) an MSA-free re-folding of the cropped pocket with the ligand to force pose resolution from biophysical complementarity rather than evolutionary alignment bias.

3 From the refined co-folded complex, the method extracts Boltz-2 internal structural representations (single/token features, pairwise interaction trunk, and a complex distogram), then fuses them with global evolutionary context (ESM3 residue embeddings) and ligand chemistry priors (Uni-Mol2 3D embedding + Morgan fingerprints).

4 The interaction module is geometry-conditioned and uses a 4-block Pairformer stack with attention/message passing masked to focus on protein–ligand (and ligand–ligand) interactions; it is initialized from the pretrained Boltz-2 affinity head so the downstream model inherits thermodynamic priors while being trained for catalytic specificity labels.

5 Training/evaluation uses ESIBank (323,783 curated pairs; 8,124 enzymes; 34,417 substrates) with hard negatives generated via EC-hierarchy sampling, and two validation regimes: random split and a stringent “unknown substrate and enzyme” split where neither enzyme nor substrate identities overlap between train and test.

6 On ESIBank, Boltz2ESI reports higher performance than sequence-only ESP and structure+docking EZSpecificity, including under the “unknown substrate and enzyme” split (AUROC 0.7664 vs 0.7198 for EZSpecificity and 0.6778 for ESP). Zero-shot Boltz-2 affinity is near-random (AUROC ~0.53), supporting the paper’s point that binding affinity alone does not determine catalytic specificity.

7 Stratifying decoys by shared EC digits, Boltz2ESI maintains stronger discriminative resolution down to deep EC levels (including enzymes sharing the same four-digit EC), suggesting the co-folded geometry helps separate tight sub-family specificities that sequence similarity and rigid scaffolds often miss.

8 Ablations attribute complementary roles to modalities: removing ESM3 embeddings causes the largest single drop (AUROC to 0.6605, AUPR to 0.2100 on the hard split), while replacing co-folded complexes with AlphaFold2/AlphaFill + AutoDock-GPU docking poses collapses precision (AUPR 0.3331 to 0.2169), highlighting that complex quality and induced-fit modeling are key for high-precision substrate discrimination.

9 A mechanistic case study on citrate synthase (large ligand-dependent domain closure) shows co-folding better recovers the catalytically competent closed-like geometry than rigid docking; the resulting Boltz2ESI score is much higher for the co-folded complex (0.9770) than for the rigid-docked setup (0.6860) when the enzyme is held out from training.

10 In an external pathway task (withanolide biosynthesis), Boltz2ESI is used to rank 107 candidate plant P450s from transcriptome data without pathway-specific training: it ranks CYP87G1 8th and CYP88C7 4th (better than EnzymeCAGE’s 13th and 10th), but ranks CYP749B2 17th (worse than EnzymeCAGE’s 6th), which the authors attribute to a more complex multi-step transformation and/or training-data coverage effects.

content:
最近は、「これ生成AIだな」と分かる文章を送ってくる人が増えている。文章はきれいに整っているのに妥当性の低さにげんなりすることも多い。

生成AIに『使われてしまっている人』は、AIへのインプットと、出力された内容のレビューがまだまだ不十分なのだと思う。

自分自身が考えること自体をサボってしまえば、AIを使うつもりが、いつの間にかAIに使われてしまう。

そのうち、指示する側から「もうあなたを介さず、AIに直接聞いた方が早い」と思われかねない。

これは由々しき事態だと思う。

重要なのは、AIへの指示を設計する力と、生成物の妥当性を判断しつつ自身の専門性を生かして修正する力。

そして、これらは生成AIをただ使い続けるだけで、自然に身につくものではない。

日頃からAIを使い倒しているだけで『AIを使える』と思い込んでしまうのはかなり危ない。

結局は、本人の問題解決能力や専門性を、日々じわじわと鍛え続けるしかないのだと思う。

昨今、AIに仕事を奪われる不安みたいなものが社会に漂っているけど、AIに代替されない領域を探し続けるより、AIを使いこなせるだけの専門性と思考力を身につける方が、ずっと安全な道だと思う。

content:
✨被災地の救世主になるか？✨

WOTA BOX（ウォータ・ボックス）は、WOTA株式会社が開発・販売するポータブル水再生システム（可搬型水再生プラント）です。

水道がない場所でも、排水の大部分をその場で浄化・再生して循環利用できる点が特徴で
「誰でもどこでも水の自由を」というミッションのもと、主に災害時の入浴支援やアウトドア・イベント用途で活用されています。

〜主な特徴〜

【高い水再生率】

生活排水（主にシャワーなどのグレーウォーター）の約98%を再生・循環利用可能。

初期水100リットルで、約100人が一人ずつシャワーを浴びられる（通常なら2人分程度の水量）
  
再生率や利用可能人数は、汚れ具合や原水の状態で変動する場合があります。

【可搬性と迅速な設置】

キャスター付きで持ち運びやすく、専門的な配管工事は不要。テント（屋外シャワーキット）と一式を大人2人で約15分程度で設営可能。

ワンボックスカーなどで輸送でき、電源と初期水があればすぐに使えます。 
 
設置スペースはおおむね平坦な場所で約4m×2m程度が目安です。

【安全性と水質管理】

活性炭フィルターとRO膜（逆浸透膜）を含む合計6つのフィルターで不純物・細菌・ウイルスを除去。
  
深紫外線（Deep-UV）照射と塩素系消毒剤の投入により、細菌・ウイルスを99.9999%以上除菌。  

AIと複数の独自センサーを組み合わせた自律制御システム（WOTA CORE）が水質とシステムを常時監視・制御。異常時は通知し、必要に応じて停止します。  

浄化された水は公衆浴場の水質基準（上り用湯・上り用水）に準拠。

WHOの飲料水ガイドラインに近い安全性を持つとの説明もありますが、飲用は想定されていません（口や目に少量入っても問題ないレベル）

【使いやすさ】

フロントディスプレイがフィルター交換タイミングや方法を案内。

石鹸・シャンプー・ボディソープも使用可能（指定のもの推奨の場合あり）

シャワー流量は約4L/分で、節水ヘッドにより家庭用と近い浴び心地です。

主な仕様（公表情報より。変更の可能性あり）

サイズ　約幅82cm × 奥行き45cm × 高さ84〜93cm程度 
 
重量　乾燥時約60〜82kg  
電源　100V AC（50/60Hz）
最大消費電力　約700W（平均400〜500W程度）
バッテリーや発電機でも使用可能。  
給湯　別途灯油式などの給湯システムを組み合わせる場合あり（灯油約5.25L/時など）
メンテナンス　使用状況によるが、フィルターはおおむねシャワー50回程度ごとに交換が必要なものが中心（所要時間約10分程度）定期的な清掃も必要

【主な活用シーン】

災害時　避難所や仮設住宅での入浴支援。水道復旧に時間がかかるケースで特に有効。

令和6年能登半島地震では石川県の複数市町に約100台が展開され、長期断水下で活用されました。

過去の地震・豪雨・台風でも多数導入実績があります。  

災害時の衛生確保や水資源の有効活用に貢献する先進的な製品として、注目されています。

皆様はどう思いましたか？？？

content:
過去に何度も説明していますが、現在は、画像認識と画像生成が同じ基盤や学習表現を共有するマルチモーダルAIが増えています。

そのため、著名な作品を画像認識するために得た知識が画像生成にも影響し、意図せず特定作品の再現度が高くなる場合があります。大手のAIサービスは、こうした酷似画像が出力されにくいよう、ガードレールを設けて対処しています。

ただし、新しいモデルでは調整が追いつかず、ガードレールが十分に機能しないこともあります。これは現在の技術が抱える課題ですが、出力された画像を確認せず、そのまま公開してよい理由にはなりません。

問題のある画像を選び、公開したのであれば、基本的には公開した利用者の責任です。AIを使ったからといって、著作権侵害の責任から逃れられるわけではありません。

これはワシ個人の好き嫌いで言っているのではありません。各国の司法でも、個別の生成物や利用行為が問題になることはあっても、それだけを理由に、AIの学習そのものを全面的に否定する判断にはつながっていません。

特にローカルAIは、ガードレールが入っていないモデルも少なくありません。自由度が高いぶん、出力内容の確認と利用判断は完全に自己責任です。

AIが出したから仕方がない、ではありません。何を生成し、何を選び、どこに公開するのか。その最終判断をした人間が責任を負うのが基本です。

title: Apple files motion for preliminary injunction against OpenAI in trade secrets case
content: Apple filed a motion on Monday asking a U.S. judge for a preliminary injunction barring two former employees, both now working for OpenAI, and OpenAI, the company that created and maintains ChatGPT, from accessing, acquiring, using or disclosing alleged confidential information as ‌it moves ahead with its trade secrets case. Last month Apple sued OpenAI and its two former employees claiming that there was a misappropriation of Apple’s trade secrets and that those trade secrets benefitted the ChatGPT owner’s ​breakout into consumer hardware. The foundation of Apple’s case rests on the assertion that OpenAI’s recruitment process for the two former employees doubled as a way to collect Apple’s proprietary information. In addition, Apple claimed that it would be ” irreparably harmed absent a preliminary injunction.” Apple also filed a motion for expedited discovery on Monday, including production of documents relating to the defendants’ alleged access ​of Apple’s confidential information. Apple included three reasons for the expedited discovery in their filing: So that Apple may: (1) better understand the nature and extent of their trade secret misappropriations and breaches of their confidentiality obligations, and the steps needed to remediate them; (2) Make additional or modified requests for injunctive relief as needed to match the facts about Defendants’ misappropriations and breaches as they are discovered; and (3) Provide the Court with a more fulsome record as needed to draft and enforce any order resulting from Apple’s concurrently filed motion for a preliminary injunction. author: Ella Phillips | U. Pittsburgh School of Law, US

title: European Commission tightens oversight on AI companies to combat deepfakes and cyber threats
content: The European Commission on Friday announced that its AI Office in Brussels and national regulators will begin enforcing key provisions of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, including new duties to identify deepfakes, label AI-generated material and oversee risks linked to powerful AI systems. This move gives EU regulators greater power to inspect advanced AI models, demand technical records and act against companies that fail to label synthetic content or control serious cyber risks.The larger team will investigate whether companies operating in the EU are operating in strict compliance with the Artificial Intelligence Act . Officials may seek technical records, examine how models work, question company staff and order changes where systems fail to meet legal requirements. The Commission has also created confidential channels for employees and users to report suspected violations. This latest development comes as European regulators have started paying closer attention to the plethora of security risks created by increasingly capable AI agents. OpenAI and Anthropic recently informed EU officials about separate cases involving unauthorized cyber activity by AI systems. The incidents have added to concerns that safety controls must continue after a model is released, rather than ending at the testing stage. Article 50 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 requires that people be informed when they are interacting with certain AI systems. It also requires providers to make AI-generated or manipulated material detectable in a machine-readable form. Those using AI to produce realistic images, audio or video must disclose when the material has been artificially created or altered. However, it must be noted that this law does not impose a blanket ban on all deepfakes. Its purpose is to simply make synthetic content easier to identify and to reduce the risk of fraud, impersonation and manipulation. title: Rights group warns India’s weapons exports to Israel may violate international law
content: Amnesty International on Thursday warned that India’s weapons exports to Israel may violate international law and contribute to the ongoing genocide in Gaza. In an investigative report , Amnesty International examined public trade data to assess the scope of India’s material support for Israel and for “international crimes committed against Palestinians in Gaza.” It found that, despite international warnings of the possible commission of war crimes , crimes against humanity and genocide in Gaza, “corporations in India have continued to export weapons, ammunitions, parts and components” to Israel. The report also emphasized that the Indian government had “failed to regulate arms exports to Israel by private companies,” and has on the contrary, strengthened its defense partnership with Israel. It detailed that, since October 7, 2023 , which was the start of the Gaza war , triggered by a coordinated cross-border assault by Hamas forces into southern Israel, Indian companies have supplied at least 390,516 small arms parts for military-grade weapons, 564,970 parts for explosive ordnance such as drone warheads, and 298 components for military vehicles to Israeli forces. Amnesty International clarified that it excluded shipments which were likely intended for anti-missile defense and civilian use. Many countries have enacted arms embargoes against Israel or limited defense cooperation with the country. In September 2025, Spain announced a total arms embargo with the aim of “stopping the genocide in Gaza”. Rights groups, including Amnesty International, have also put forth proposals for arms bans and embargoes in an effort to put pressure on Israel and prevent genocide. The UN has also warned that arms trading with Israel may be unlawful. title: UN High Commissioner warns of deepening peril for civil liberties as Uganda tightens restrictions
content: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk on Thursday condemned the growing crackdown on fundamental freedoms in Uganda, raising concerns about the erosion of the rule of law in the country and increasing military involvement in civilian institutions, which contribute to a shrinking of civic space. In commenting on the current state of domestic affairs within the country, Türk stated: “I am appalled that the authorities are increasingly targeting any form of dissent, and deepening restrictions on the fundamental freedoms of all those living in Uganda…” He added that the authorities’ actions are fostering a climate of fear among citizens, which increases self-censorship and further restricts public debate, thereby deepening polarisation. The UN reported that repression against opposition figures in Uganda has escalated since the general elections that were held on January 15. Based on information received by the UN Human Rights Office, at least 50 opposition figures, five human rights defenders, and five journalists have experienced various human rights violations, including enforced disappearances, arbitrary arrests, torture, and ill-treatment. The Human Rights Office has also stated that it had information about increased military involvement in the functions of civilian institutions, with some media outlets forced to close temporarily. Furthermore, Türk criticised the promulgation of special legislation that targets civic space by imposing restrictions on engagement with civil society organizations and international funding, such as the Protection of Sovereignty Act enacted in May 2026. This bill monitors the political activity of foreign actors, regulations foreign funding, and establishes a registration system for any person deemed an “agent of a foreigner.” Rights organizations have previously criticized the Act for its broad provisions and for limiting freedom of speech and peaceful assembly. title: Amnesty International warns Nicaragua constitutional reform dismantles right to public participation
content: Amnesty International on Thursday raised alarm after Nicaragua’s announcement of a constitutional reform initiative that threatens to erase the country’s remaining democratic safeguards, extending presidential terms and permanently barring opponents from elections. President Daniel Ortega and co‑president Rosario Murillo have been accused of widespread abuses , from jailing critics to stripping political opponents of their possessions. President Daniel Ortega called for extending presidential terms from six years to seven years., and bar opposition candidates, claiming that the opposition is controlled by the United States. During a speech last Sunday at an event commemorating the 1979 Sandinista revolution , President Ortega said: “There won’t be ⁠⁠any more elections here for them to try to seize the government and seize power.” President Ortega, now ruling with his wife the “co-president” Rosario Murillo, has been in power since 2007. Murillo was formally designated her position in government following constitutional changes in 2024. On Tuesday, Congress President Gustavo Porras offered a preview of the constitutional reform’s content, according to several media reports, though he withheld substantive details. The measure, which is slated for approval in September, comes on the heels of recent remarks by the president asserting that elections would no longer be held in Nicaragua, a move aimed at preventing the opposition from “seizing the government.” Other governments around the world have since denounced President Ortega’s statement that Nicaragua will no longer hold free elections, urging the country to comply with democratic principles in fears that it will lead to an unprecedented level of authoritarian control. Nicaragua is a state party to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), having acceded to it on March 12, 1980. title: Ceuta border surge leaves 34 dead as mass crossing tests refugee convention obligations
content: A mass border breach at Spain’s North African enclave of Ceuta on Friday has left at least 34 people dead after an estimated 60,000 attempted to cross into the territory, sparking what officials describe as a deepening border crisis. Spanish Prime Minster Pedro Sánchez condemned the crossings as a “violation of Spain’s territorial sovereignty,” and pledged full support to Ceuta authorities. Spain has reinforced the enclave with soldiers and police, while Morocco deployed water cannons to push back crowds. Spain’s Interior Ministry has reported that more than 25,000 migrants have been returned to Morocco, at a shocking rate of 150 per minute. Migrants attempted crossings by swimming from Moroccan towns like Fnideq (five kilometers) or Belyounech (a shorter distance), or by climbing border fences. Authorities attributed the latest surge in migrant crossings to a Spanish Supreme Court ruling that barred immediate returns of migrants intercepted at sea without due process. The ruling does not apply to land entries. Some Moroccan migrant rights activists questioned this explanation, arguing that most migrants were likely unaware of the judgment and thus, could not have factored it into their decision to cross using the sea route. Ceuta is a Spanish autonomous city on Africa’s north coast, bordering Morocco. Along with along with the nearby Spanish enclave of Melilla, it forms one of only two EU land borders with Africa. They have been under Spanish sovereignty since 1580. After African decolonization, Ceuta and Melilla remained the only European-held territories on the mainland of Africa. Ceuta’s location makes it a key entry point for migrants and asylum seekers trying to reach Europe. The enclave is heavily fortified with fences, surveillance, and a permanent border police and Civil Guard presence. title: Trump blames Tim Walz for water hacks even though it’s probably Iran

title: Tomorrow’s U.S. Senate Vote: Four Internet Bills, One Wrong Direction
content: The Senate Commerce Committee will vote this week on several censorious and privacy invasive bills: KOSA , the SCREEN Act , Youth AI Privacy Act, and CHATBOT Act . While we appreciate that the Committee is taking the time to look at these bills separately, it’s still impossible to ignore the message Congress is sending to the world: Age-gate the internet and block young people from speaking and accessing lawful speech online. Or else. Take action Tell Congress: don't age-gate the internet Each of these bills claims to be trying to protect children and teenagers from dangerous situations on and offline—certainly a worthy goal. But the proposed solutions in these bills are unlikely to make children and teenagers safer at all. Rather, they would create sweeping new privacy and data security problems, and force platforms to adopt unconstitutional restrictions on the content they host, for both adults and teenagers. There is a better way. Instead of considering these bills, the Senate Commerce Committee should be focusing on a national consumer privacy bill that would protect ALL internet users, or on banning behavioral advertising that tracks us across the web—again, for users of all ages. But the bills being considered this week move in the other direction—more information being collected, more surveillance, and less privacy for internet users of all ages. Take action help eff oppose these bills EFF sent a letter to the Committee with our concerns about these bills. We look forward to continuing to work with them to find a way forward that protects all users.
author: India McKinney

title: Appeals Court Agrees with EFF that Building a Web Browser Doesn’t Violate the CFAA
content: The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals has endorsed a commonsense technical interpretation of the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA), a law not usually given to such interpretation. Amazon had sued Perplexity AI to try to shut down its Comet browser, claiming the browser’s optional agentic AI “Assistant” that can browse websites like Amazon for comparison shopping purposes, violated the CFAA because Amazon did not “authorize” Perplexity to access Amazon users’ accounts. Rejecting that theory, the Ninth Circuit held that Perplexity was unlikely to be liable because users operate the tool, not Perplexity. That’s the right conclusion, as both a legal and technical matter. As we explained to the court in our amicus brief , the CFAA requires unauthorized “access,” and Perplexity itself does not access Amazon’s servers—users of the Comet browser do. The court agreed, noting that EFF’s explanation “articulates the nature of the system most clearly.” The court noted that agentic AI may present novel legal issues, and there is “little to no existing caselaw directly dealing with how to ascribe responsibility for AI agents like the Assistant, let alone caselaw specifically dealing with agentic AI in the CFAA context.” Ultimately, though, thorny questions of AI “intent” were irrelevant to this case, because the Assistant “is a tool, not a person for statutory purposes.” And, the court concluded, it is a tool operated by users, not Perplexity. Even where Perplexity received information from users about their Amazon accounts and used this information to instruct the Assistant, the court found that that did not constitute the sort of control needed to find access by Perplexity. As the court noted, Amazon might have other viable claims against Perplexity, but invoking the CFAA was both legally baseless and bad policy that “could expose users themselves to criminal liability. This is a gratifying decision because all too often, big players use the CFAA to bully upstarts and innovators
author: Andrew Crocker

title: Mobile Ad Software Encourages Location Data Sharing, EFF Report Finds
content: Developers Must Beware of Ad Libraries that Betray Users’ Privacy SAN FRANCISCO – Some software development kits (SDKs) provided by advertising companies to help developers monetize their apps are automatically feeding users’ location data into systems that location data brokers use to track people, an Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) report found . EFF began investigating the location-sharing practices of various advertising SDKs to better understand the pipeline from mobile apps to location data brokers. The probe revealed how such SDKs can facilitate and encourage location data sharing – without users’ knowledge or meaningful consent – through privacy-invasive defaults, financial incentives, and unclear documentation. “Defaults matter, not just for users, but for app developers as well. If app developers don’t pay close attention to the location-sharing settings of their advertising tools, they could inadvertently expose users’ location information,” EFF Staff Technologist Lena Cohen said. “Users can take extra steps to defend their location privacy, but they shouldn’t have to. Developers, regulators, and legislators must act to stop apps from leaking users’ location to advertising companies and data brokers.” Cohen and EFF Senior Staff Technologist Bill Budington reviewed the public developer documentation of dozens of widely used advertising SDKs to identify how they handle and communicate with developers about location data. In their analysis, they highlighted four advertising SDKs that collect and share a user's location by default for ad targeting whenever the user has given the app location permissions: InMobi, BidMachine, Verve’s HyBid, and Huawei’s Petal Ads. But EFF’s focus on these four does not mean that other SDKs adequately protect location data or that developers never choose to share location data when it’s not the default. title: Developers: Beware of Ad Libraries that Betray Your Users’ Location Privacy
content: Across mobile platforms, advertising companies provide developers with software development kits (SDKs) that make it easy to monetize their apps. But those same SDKs can automatically feed users’ location data into ad systems that location data brokers use to track people. Many developers may not even be aware of this privacy violation, let alone the users who are directly affected. When developers let advertising SDKs collect location data, they’re putting users at risk of more than just creepy ads. Location information sourced from the advertising industry has been used for ICE investigations , global spy tools , outing a gay priest , tracking union organizers , and tracking US military personnel . Defaults matter, not just for users, but for app developers as well. An EFF investigation has identified several advertising SDKs that publicly acknowledge collecting and sharing users’ location by default when embedded in Android apps granted location permissions. Defaults matter, not just for users, but for app developers as well. If app developers don’t pay close attention to the location-sharing settings of their advertising tools, they could inadvertently expose users’ location information. This report explains how advertising SDKs can facilitate and encourage location data sharing through privacy-invasive defaults, financial incentives, and unclear documentation.
